BitField.description:
WDT 0 Reset Flag
The WDT 0 reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer 0 or Window Watchdog Timer 0 to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer 0 register RSTF(WDT0_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT 0 time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer 0 register WWDTRF(WWDT0_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT 0 time-out reset.
BitField.name: WDT0RF

BitField.description: LVR Reset Flag\nThe LVR reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Low Voltage Reset Controller to indicate the previous reset source.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: LVRF

BitField.description: Cortex-A35 Core 0 Debug Reset Flag\nThe Cortex-A35 core 0 debug reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from DBGRSTREQ of Cortex-A35 core 0 to indicate the previous reset source.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPU0DBGRF

BitField.description: Cortex-A35 Core 0 Warm Reset Flag\nThe Cortex-A35 core 0 warm reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from WARMRSTREQ of Cortex-A35 core 0 to indicate the previous reset source. The WARMRSTREQ of Cortex-A35 core 0 trigger by writing 1 to the bit RR (RMR[1], Reset Management Register of Cortex-A35 core 0)\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPU0WARMRF

BitField.description: HRESET Reset Flag\nThe HRESET reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the HRESET.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: HRESETRF

BitField.description: CPU 0 Reset Flag\nThe CPU 0 reset flag is set by hardware if software writes CA35CR0RST (SYS_IPRST0[1]) 1 to reset Cortex-A35 Core 0.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPU0RF

BitField.description:
WDT 1 Reset Flag
The WDT 1 reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer 1 or Window Watchdog Timer 1 to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer 1 register RSTF (WDT1_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT 1 time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer 1 register WWDTRF (WWDT1_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT 1 time-out reset.
Note 3: This flag only take effect when WDT1RSTAEN (SYS_MISCRFCR[16]) is 1.
BitField.name: WDT1RF

BitField.description:
WDT 2 Reset Flag for Cortex-A35
The WDT 2 reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer 2 or Window Watchdog Timer 2 to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer 2 register RSTF(WDT2_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT 2 time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer 2 register WWDTRF(WWDT2_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT 2 time-out reset.
Note 3: This flag only take effect when WDT2RSTAEN (SYS_MISCRFCR[17]) is 1.
BitField.name: WDT2RFA

BitField.description: Cortex-A35 Core 1 Debug Reset Flag\nThe Cortex-A35 core 1 debug reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from DBGRSTREQ of Cortex-A35 core 1 to indicate the previous reset source.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPU1DBGRF

BitField.description: Cortex-A35 Core 1 Warm Reset Flag\nThe Cortex-A35 core 1 warm reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from WARMRSTREQ of Cortex-A35 core 1 to indicate the previous reset source. The WARMRSTREQ of Cortex-A35 core 1 trigger by writing 1 to the bit RR (RMR[1], Reset Management Register of Cortex-A35 core 1)\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPU1WARMRF

BitField.description: Cortex-A35 Core 1 Reset Flag\nThe Cortex-A35 Core 1 reset flag is set by hardware if software writes CA35CR1RST (SYS_IPRST0[2]) 1 to reset Cortex-A35 Core 1.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPU1RF

BitField.description:
WDT 1 Reset Flag for RTP Cortex-M4
The WDT 1 reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer 1 or Window Watchdog Timer 1 to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer 1 register RSTF(WDT1_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT 1 time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer 1 register WWDTRF(WWDT1_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT 1 time-out reset.
Note 3: This flag only take effect when WDT1RSTMEN (SYS_MISCRFCR[18]) is 1.
BitField.name: WDT1RFM

BitField.description:
WDT 2 Reset Flag for RTP Cortex-M4
The WDT 2 reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer 2 or Window Watchdog Timer 2 to indicate the previous reset source.

Note 2: Watchdog Timer 2 register RSTF(WDT2_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT 2 time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer 2 register WWDTRF(WWDT2_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT 2 time-out reset.
BitField.name: WDT2RF

BitField.description: RTP M4 CPU Lockup Reset Flag\nNote 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.\nNote 2: When CPU lockup happened under ICE is connected, this flag will set to 1 but chip will not reset.
BitField.name: RTPM4LKRF

BitField.description: RTP M4 System Reset Flag\nThe system reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Cortex-M4 Core to indicate the previous reset source.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: RTPM4SYSRF

BitField.description: RTP PMU System Reset Flag\nThe system reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the PMU of Cortex-M4 Core to indicate the previous reset source.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: RTPPMUSYSRF

BitField.description: RTP M4 CPU Reset Flag\nThe RTP M4 CPU reset flag is set by hardware if software writes CM4RST (SYS_IPRST0[3]) 1 to reset Cortex-M4 Core.\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: RTPM4CPURF

BitField.description:
Power-on-reset Disable Code (Write Protect)
When powered on, the Power-On-Reset (POR) circuit generates a reset signal to reset whole chip function. However, after power is ready, the POR circuit would consume a few power. To minimize the POR circuit power consumption, user to disable POR circuit by writing 0x5AA5 to this field.
The POR circuit will become active again when this field is set to other value or chip is reset by other reset source, including /RESET pin, Watchdog, LVR reset and the software chip reset function.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: PORDISCODE

BitField.description:
Wake-up Delay Counter Enable Bit (Write Protect)
When the Cortex-A35 wakes up from Power-down mode, the clock control will delay certain clock cycles to wait system clock stable.
The delayed clock cycle is 4096 clock cycles when chip works at 24 Mhz external high speed crystal oscillator (HXT), and 256 clock cycles when chip works at 12 MHz internal high speed RC oscillator (HIRC).
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: PDWKDLY

BitField.name: PWRSTBTM

BitField.name: PWRACKTO

BitField.description:
Cortex-A35 Power Down Enable Bit (Write Protect)
When this bit is set to 1, Power-down mode is enabled and the chip keeps active till the CPU sleep mode is also active and then the chip enters Power-down mode.
When chip wakes up from Power-down mode, this bit is auto cleared. Users need to set this bit again for next Power-down.
In Power-down mode, HXT, HIRC, PLL and system clock will be disabled and ignored the clock source selection. The clocks of peripheral are not controlled by Power-down mode, if the peripheral clock source is from LXT or LIRC.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: A35PDEN

BitField.description: Cortex-A35 Entering Power-down Even ICE Connected (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: A35DBPDEN

BitField.description:
RTP M4 Power Down Enable (Write Protect, SubM)
When this bit is set to 1, Power-down mode is enabled and the chip keeps active till the CPU sleep mode is also active and then the chip enters Power-down mode.
When chip wakes up from Power-down mode, this bit is auto cleared. Users need to set this bit again for next Power-down.
In Power-down mode, HXT, HIRC, PLL and system clock will be disabled and ignored the clock source selection. The clocks of peripheral are not controlled by Power-down mode, if the peripheral clock source is from LXT or LIRC.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: RTPPDEN

BitField.description:
DDR Controller Core Clock Gating Disable Bit (TZNS)
Note: This register needs to be set to 1'b1 to bypass clock gating function of DDR core clock before user writes/reads control registers or status registers of DDR memory controller.
Therefore the signals in PCLK domain of DDR memory controller can be synchronous to core clock domain of DDR memory controller, and the signals in core clock domain of DDR memory controller can be synchronous to PCLK domain of DDR memory controller correctly.
After user writes/reads control registers or status registers of DDR memory controller, this register can be set to 1'b0 to enable clock gating function of DDR core clock.
BitField.name: DDRCGDIS

BitField.description:
DDR Auto Self Refresh Delay Count (TZNS)
This register uses to set the delay cycles of DDR memory controller before the core clock of DDR memory controller is gating. It allows for the self-refresh status to propagate to the APB domain so the STAT.selfref_type register field also reflects the status. 
It is sufficient to set this delay cycles to 31 cycles normally. In particular, if the AXI frequency is much less than the DDRC frequency, a higher value may be required in order to ensure that all read data is synchronized to the AXI domain before the clock is removed.
Note: User can set this register value during core reset of DDR memory controller is asserted (i.e. MCTLCRST (SYS_IPRST0[29]) set to 1'b1).
BitField.name: DRATSRDLY

BitField.description:
Register Lock Control Code (Write Only)
Some registers have write-protection function. Writing these registers have to disable the protected function by writing the sequence value "59h", "16h", "88h" to this field. After this sequence is completed, the REGLCTL bit will be set to 1 and write-protection registers can be normal write.

REGLCTL[0]
Register Lock Control Disable Index (Read Only)
BitField.name: REGLCTL

BitField.description: HXT Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: HXT cannot be disabled and HXTEN will always read as 1 if HCLK clock source is selected from HXT or PLL (clock source from HXT).
BitField.name: HXTEN

BitField.description: LXT Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: LXT cannot be disabled and LXTEN will always read as 1 if HCLK clock source is selected from LXT when the LXT clock source is selected as external LXT by setting C32KS(RTC_LXTCTL[6]) to 1.
BitField.name: LXTEN

BitField.description:
HIRC Enable Bit (Write Protect)
The HCLK default clock source is from HIRC and this bit default value is 1.
Note 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
Note 2: HIRC cannot be disabled and HIRCEN will always read as 1 if HXTFQIEN or is set.
BitField.name: HIRCEN

BitField.description: LIRC Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: LIRCEN

BitField.description: HXT Drive Current Strength (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: HXTDS

BitField.description: SYSPLL Auto Power Down Option when CA35 and RTP-M4 are Power Down (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 and RTP-M4 and TSI-M4 are not all in Power-down mode. If one of RTP-M4 , CA35, or TSI-M4 is not in Power-down mode, the PLL PD pin status is controlled by CLK_PLLCTL [16] in Crypto Sub System.
BitField.name: SYSPLLAPD

BitField.description: CAPLL Auto Power Down Option when CA35 is Power Gating (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 core power is not ready. If CA35 core power is ready, the PLL PD pin status is controlled by CLK_PLL0CTL1[0].
BitField.name: CAPLLAPD

BitField.description: DDRPLL Auto Power Down Option when CA35 is Power Gating (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 core power is not ready. If CA35 core power is ready, the PLL PD pin status is controlled by CLK_PLL2CTL1[0].
BitField.name: DDRPLLAPD

BitField.description: HXT Auto Off Option when CA35 is Power Gating (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 core power is not ready. If CA35 core power is ready, the HXT enable bit is controlled by CLK_PWRCTL[0].
BitField.name: HXTAOFF

BitField.description: HIRC Auto Off Option when CA35 is Power Gating (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 core power is not ready. If CA35 core power is ready, the HIRC enable bit is controlled by CLK_PWRCTL[2].
BitField.name: HIRCAOFF

BitField.description: LXT Stable Count Select (Write Protect)\nNote: These bits are write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: LXTSTBS

BitField.description: GIC CLK Auto Off Option when CA35 is Power Gating (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 core power is not ready. If CA35 core power is ready, the HIRC enable bit is controlled by CLK_PWRCTL[2].
BitField.name: GICAOFF

BitField.description: HXT Auto Off Option when CA35 is Power Down (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 cores are in the WFI. If CA35 cores are not in WFI, the HXT enable bit is controlled by CLK_PWRCTL[0].
BitField.name: HXTAPD

BitField.description: HIRC Auto Off Option when CA35 is Power Down (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.\nNote 2: This bit only works when the CA35 cores are in the WFI. If CA35 cores are not in WFI, the HIRC enable bit is controlled by CLK_PWRCTL[2].
BitField.name: HIRCAPD

BitField.name: FBDIV

BitField.description: PLL Input Divider Control (Write Protect)\nRefer to the formulas at PLL Control Mode. This register is referring to the parameter M.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: INDIV

BitField.description: PLL Output Divider Control (Write Protect)\nRefer to the formulas at PLL Control Mode. This register is referring to the parameter P.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: OUTDIV

BitField.description: Power-down Mode (Write Protect)\nIf set the PDEN bit to 1 in CLK_PWRCTL register, the PLL will enter Power-down mode, too.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: PD

BitField.description: PLL Bypass Control (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register.
BitField.name: BP

BitField.description: PLL Feedback Divider Control (Write Protect)\nSet the feedback divider factor (N) from 16 to 2047.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: FBDIV

BitField.description: PLL Reference Input Divider Control (Write Protect)\nSet the reference divider factor (M) from 1 to 63.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: INDIV

BitField.description:
Operation Mode Selection (Write Protect)
This mode is suitable for in output frequency of PLL will be modulated by triangle wave. It is for EMI consideration.
By setting SSRATE [10:0] and SLOPE [23:0], the modulation index and the modulation frequency can be programmed. Refer to the formulas at Advanced PLL Spread Spectrum Mode.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: MODE

BitField.description: Spreading Frequency Control (Write Protect)\nSet the spread step factor SSRATE from 0 to 2047, \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: SSRATE

BitField.description: Power-down Mode (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: PD

BitField.description: PLL Bypass Control (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: BP

BitField.description: PLL Output Divider Control (Write Protect)\nSet the output divider factor (P) from 1 to 7.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: OUTDIV

BitField.description: PLL Fractional Portion of DN Value (Write Protect)\nSet the fraction part (X) of Fractional Portion of DN Value factor.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: FRAC

BitField.description: PLL Stable Counter Selection (Write Protect)\nSet the spread step factor SLOPE from 0 to 16777215, \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register. For PLL3, PLL4, and PLL5, user can also refer to the SYS_RLKTZNS register if SYSSIAEN is 1.
BitField.name: SLOPE

BitField.description:
Set SRAM0 Security Boundary
Set the 16 Kbytes-aligned boundary of SRAM0.
The SRAM part below the boundary is SubM region and the part higher the boundary is ShareMemory region.
When the boundary is set to higher than the size of SRAM, the whole SRAM is SubM region.
BitField.name: SR0BOUND

BitField.description:
Set SRAM1 Security Boundary
Set the 16 Kbytes-aligned boundary of data SRAM.
The SRAM part below the boundary is TZS region and the part higher the boundary is TZNS region.
When the boundary is set to higher than the size of SRAM, the whole SRAM is TZS region.
BitField.name: SR1BOUND

Register.description: Provides information about the configuration of the TZC-400.
Register.name: TZC0_BUILD_CONFIG

BitField.description: Defines the number of regions that the TZC-400 provides:0b01000 Nine regionsAll other values Reserved.
BitField.name: no_of_regions

Register.description: Controls the interrupt and bus response signaling behavior of the TZC-400 when region permission failures occur.
Register.name: TZC0_ACTION

Register.description: Provides control and status for the gate keeper in each filter unit implemented
Register.name: TZC0_GATE_KEEPER

BitField.description:
Each bit in this field requests the gate of the associated filter unit to be open or closed Each bit is associated as follows:bit 0 Filter 0 
bit 1 Filter 1 
bit 2 Filter 2 
bit 3 Filter 3.
Set the open_request bit to 1, to request the gate to be open Set the open_request bit to 0, to request the gate to be closedIf any of the associated filter units are not implemented, the corresponding open_request bits are unused,
BitField.name: open_request

BitField.description: The current state of the gate keeper in each filter unit The bit associations are as follows:bit 16 Filter 0 gate keeper status bit 17 Filter 1 gate keeper status bit 18 Filter 2 gate keeper status bit 19 Filter 3 gate keeper statusWhen a bit is set to 1, the gate keeper permits access to its associated filter, that is, it is openWhen a bit is set to 0, the gate keeper no longer permits access to its associated filter, that is, it is closed This bit is set to 0 when both of the following conditions are fulfilled:This means that the gate keeper always waits for outstanding accesses to complete•The gate keeper no longer permits access to its associated filter\n•All outstanding accesses through the filter unit are complete\nIf any of the associated filter units are not implemented, the corresponding gate keeper bits are unused,
BitField.name: open_status

Register.description: Controls the read access speculation and write access speculation.
Register.name: TZC0_SPECULATION_CTRL

BitField.description:
Controlsread access speculation
Note:This bit is ignored and assumed to be zero at a filter unit if the corresponding QVNENABLE<x> signal is HIGH
You can set this bit as follows:
BitField.name: read_spec_disable

BitField.description: Set this bit as follows: \nNote:This bit is ignored and assumed to be zero at a filter unit if the corresponding QVNE NABLE<x.
BitField.name: write_spec_disable

Register.description: Contains the status of the interrupt signal, TZCINT, that reports access security violations or region overlap errors.
Register.name: TZC0_INT_STATUS

BitField.description:
Each bit is associated as follows: 
bit 0 Filter 0 
bit 1 Filter 1 
bit 2 Filter 2 
bit 3 Filter 3.
BitField.name: status

BitField.description:
The bit associations are as follows: 
bit 8 Filter 0 
bit 9 Filter 1 
bit 10 Filter 2 
bit 11 Filter 3.
When a bit is set to 1, it indicates the occurrence of two or more region permission or region overlapping failures at the associated filter unit after the interrupt was cleared by the associated bit
This bit is set even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt
Clear the interrupt status of the associated bit in the INT_CLEAR register to also clear this field.
BitField.name: overrun

BitField.description:
The bit associations are as follows: 
bit 16 Filter 0 
bit 17 Filter 1 
bit 18 Filter 2 
bit 19 Filter 3
When a bit is set to 1, it indicates a violation of the overlap region configuration rules for the associated filter unit This occurs when an access matches with two enabled regions at the same time unless the overlap is only with Region 0.This bit is set even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt When this bit is 1, the interrupt status bit is also set to 1.Clear the interrupt status of the associated bit to also clear this field
BitField.name: overlap

BitField.description:
Contains the control bits to clear interrupts The bit associations are as follows: 
bit 0 Filter 0 
bit 1 Filter 1 
bit 2 Filter 2 
bit 3 Filter 3.
Write a 1 to any of these bits to clear the associated status, overrun, and overlap bits in the INT_STATUS register.
BitField.name: clear

Register.description: Contains the lower 32 bits of the address of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC0_FAIL_ADDRESS_LOW_0

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field returns the ACE-Lite address bits [31:0. You must clear the associated interrupt status before this field can return the address of accesses of subsequent permission checks or region overlap failures\nThis occurs even if the ACTION register does not enable the interrupt\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: addr_status_low

Register.description: Contains the lower 32 bits of the address of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC0_FAIL_ADDRESS_LOW_1

Register.description: Contains the lower 32 bits of the address of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. Register.description: Contains the control status information of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC0_FAIL_CONTROL_0

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field indicates whether it was an unprivileged or privileged access attempt\nYou must clear the associated interrupt status before this field can return the values of accesses of subsequent permission checks or region overlap failures\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: Privileged

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field indicates whether it was a Secure or Non- secure access attempt\nYou must clear the associated interrupt status before this field can return the direction of accesses of subsequent permission checks or region overlap failures\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: Non_secure

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field indicates whether the failed access was a read or write access attempt\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: Direction

BitField.description:
Independent region enable for each filter unit Each bit is associated with a filter unit Set these bits as follows:
Bit 0 For Filter 0 
Bit 1 For Filter 1 
Bit 2 For Filter 2 
Bit 3 For Filter 3.
When set HIGH, it enables the use of the current region programming for the associated filter For Region 0, all bits are set HIGH and cannot be modified.
BitField.name: filter_en

Register.name: TZC0_REGION_ID_ACCESS_0

BitField.description: NSAID read enables \nThis enables NSAID inputs to define Non-secure read access permission Each bit of the nsaid_rd_en register field is associated with a value on the NSAIDR<x> signal as follows:\n<x> is the filter unit number.When any bit in this field is set HIGH, TZC-400 permits Non-secure read access to any access with the associated NSAIDR<x> value. For example, if NSAIDR<x> is 3 and the corresponding nsaid_rd_en[3] bit is set HIGH then TZC-400 permits the Non-secure read access to progress.
BitField.name: nsaid_rd_en

BitField.description: NSAID write enables \n<x> is the filter unit number.\nWhen any bit in this field is set to 1, TZC-400 permits Non-secure write access to any access with theassociated NSAIDW<x> value. For example, if NSAIDW<x> is 3 and the corresponding nsaid_wr_en[3] bit is set HIGH then TZC-400 permits the Non-secure write access to progress.
BitField.name: nsaid_wr_en

BitField.description:
NSAID read enables 
This enables NSAID inputs to define Non-secure read access permission Each bit of the nsaid_rd_en register field is associated with a value on the NSAIDR<x> signal as follows:
<x> is the filter unit number.
When any bit in this field is set HIGH, TZC-400 permits Non-secure read access to any access with the associated NSAIDR<x> value. For example, if NSAIDR<x> is 3 and the corresponding nsaid_rd_en[3] bit is set HIGH then TZC-400 permits the Non-secure read access to progress.
BitField.name: nsaid_rd_en

BitField.description: NSAID write enables \n<x> is the filter unit number.\nWhen any bit in this field is set to 1, TZC-400 permits Non-secure write access to any access with theassociated NSAIDW<x> value. For example, if NSAIDW<x> is 3 and the corresponding nsaid_wr_en[3] bit is set HIGH then TZC-400 permits the Non-secure write access to progress.
BitField.name: nsaid_wr_en

BitField.description: The number of 4 Kbytes address blocks required to access the registers, expressed in powers of 2 These bits read back as 0x0 This means that the TZC-400 occupies a single 4 Kbytes address block.

Register.name: TZC0_PID0

BitField.description: These bits read back as 0x60

Register.description: The PID1 register provides the following information about the peripheral configuration:• part_number_1.• Jep106_id_3_0.
Register.name: TZC0_PID1

BitField.description: These bits read back as 0x4.
BitField.name: part_number_1

BitField.description: JEP106 identity code [3:0] See the JEP106, Standard Manufacturer Identification Code These bits read back as 0xB because ARM is the peripheral designer.
BitField.name: jep106_id_3_0

Register.description: The PID2 register provides the following information about the peripheral configuration:• Jep106_id_6_4.• Revision number.• JEDEC use flag.

BitField.description: Identifies the revision of the TZC-400 For revision r0p1, this field is set to 0x2.

BitField.description: The top-level RTL provides a 4-bit input, USERPID3REVAND, that is normally tied LOW and provides a read value of 0x0 When silicon is available, and if metal fixes are required, the manufacturer can modify the tie-offs to indicate a revision of the silicon.
BitField.name: RevAnd

Register.name: TZC2_ACTION

Register.description: Provides control and status for the gate keeper in each filter unit implemented
Register.name: TZC2_GATE_KEEPER

BitField.description:
Each bit in this field requests the gate of the associated filter unit to be open or closed Each bit is associated as follows:bit 0 Filter 0 
bit 1 Filter 1 
bit 2 Filter 2 
bit 3 Filter 3.
Set the open_request bit to 1, to request the gate to be open Set the open_request bit to 0, to request the gate to be closedIf any of the associated filter units are not implemented, the corresponding open_request bits are unused,
BitField.name: open_request

BitField.description: The current state of the gate keeper in each filter unit The bit associations are as follows:bit 16 Filter 0 gate keeper status bit 17 Filter 1 gate keeper status bit 18 Filter 2 gate keeper status bit 19 Filter 3 gate keeper statusWhen a bit is set to 1, the gate keeper permits access to its associated filter, that is, it is openWhen a bit is set to 0, the gate keeper no longer permits access to its associated filter, that is, it is closed This bit is set to 0 when both of the following conditions are fulfilled:This means that the gate keeper always waits for outstanding accesses to complete•The gate keeper no longer permits access to its associated filter\n•All outstanding accesses through the filter unit are complete\nIf any of the associated filter units are not implemented, the corresponding gate keeper bits are unused,
BitField.name: open_status

Register.description: Controls the read access speculation and write access speculation.
Register.name: TZC2_SPECULATION_CTRL

BitField.description:
Controlsread access speculation
Note:This bit is ignored and assumed to be zero at a filter unit if the corresponding QVNENABLE<x> signal is HIGH
You can set this bit as follows:
BitField.name: read_spec_disable

BitField.description: Set this bit as follows: \nNote:This bit is ignored and assumed to be zero at a filter unit if the corresponding QVNE NABLE<x.
BitField.name: write_spec_disable

Register.description: Contains the status of the interrupt signal, TZCINT, that reports access security violations or region overlap errors.
Register.name: TZC2_INT_STATUS

BitField.description:
Each bit is associated as follows: 
bit 0 Filter 0 
bit 1 Filter 1 
bit 2 Filter 2 
bit 3 Filter 3.
BitField.name: status

BitField.description:
The bit associations are as follows: 
bit 8 Filter 0 
bit 9 Filter 1 
bit 10 Filter 2 
bit 11 Filter 3.
When a bit is set to 1, it indicates the occurrence of two or more region permission or region overlapping failures at the associated filter unit after the interrupt was cleared by the associated bit
This bit is set even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt
Clear the interrupt status of the associated bit in the INT_CLEAR register to also clear this field.
BitField.name: overrun

BitField.description:
The bit associations are as follows: 
bit 16 Filter 0 
bit 17 Filter 1 
bit 18 Filter 2 
bit 19 Filter 3
When a bit is set to 1, it indicates a violation of the overlap region configuration rules for the associated filter unit This occurs when an access matches with two enabled regions at the same time unless the overlap is only with Region 0.This bit is set even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt When this bit is 1, the interrupt status bit is also set to 1.Clear the interrupt status of the associated bit to also clear this field
BitField.name: overlap

BitField.description:
Contains the control bits to clear interrupts The bit associations are as follows: 
bit 0 Filter 0 
bit 1 Filter 1 
bit 2 Filter 2 
bit 3 Filter 3.
Write a 1 to any of these bits to clear the associated status, overrun, and overlap bits in the INT_STATUS register.
BitField.name: clear

Register.description: Contains the lower 32 bits of the address of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC2_FAIL_ADDRESS_LOW_0

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field returns the ACE-Lite address bits [31:0. You must clear the associated interrupt status before this field can return the address of accesses of subsequent permission checks or region overlap failures\nThis occurs even if the ACTION register does not enable the interrupt\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: addr_status_low

Register.description: Contains the lower 32 bits of the address of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC2_FAIL_ADDRESS_LOW_1

Register.description: Contains the lower 32 bits of the address of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC2_FAIL_ADDRESS_LOW_2

Register.description: Contains the control status information of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. The first failing access is defined as the first permission failure in the associated filter unit after one of the following occurs:• Reset.• The last clearance of an interrupt using the INT_CLEAR register.
Register.name: TZC2_FAIL_CONTROL_0

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field indicates whether it was an unprivileged or privileged access attempt\nYou must clear the associated interrupt status before this field can return the values of accesses of subsequent permission checks or region overlap failures\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: Privileged

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field indicates whether it was a Secure or Non- secure access attempt\nYou must clear the associated interrupt status before this field can return the direction of accesses of subsequent permission checks or region overlap failures\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: Non_secure

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field indicates whether the failed access was a read or write access attempt\nIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.
BitField.name: Direction

Register.description: Contains the control status information of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. Register.name: TZC2_FAIL_CONTROL_1

Register.description: Contains the control status information of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. Register.description: Contains the master ACE-Lite ARID or AWID of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. This occurs even if the ACTION register is set to not drive the interrupt signal. Register.name: TZC2_FAIL_ID_0

BitField.description: If a region permission check fails or a region overlap occurs, this field returns the ACE-Lite ID values of the first failed accessIf the status flag for the filter unit in the INT_STATUS register is already set, new region permission check failures in the same filter unit do not update the associated fail status group of registers.

BitField.name: vnet

Register.description: Contains the master ACE-Lite ARID or AWID of the first access that failed a region permission check in the associated filter unit. BitField.description:
WDT Reset Flag (Read Only)
The WDT reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer or Window Watchdog Timer to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer register RSTF(WDTx_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer register WWDTRF(WWDTx_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT time-out reset.
BitField.name: WDTRF

BitField.description:
System Reset Flag (Read Only)
The system reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Cortex-M4 core to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: From Cortex-M4 side, this bit set to 1 cannot be seen.
BitField.name: SYSRF

BitField.description: CPU Reset Flag (Read Only)\nThe CPU reset flag is set by hardware if software writes CPURST (SYS_IPRST0[3:1]) 1 to reset counterpart CPU (any of A35 Core or M4 Core).\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPURF

BitField.description:
CPU Lockup Reset Flag (Read Only)
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: When CPU lockup happened under ICE is connected, this flag will set to 1 but chip will not reset.
Note 3: From Cortex-M4 side, this bit set to 1 cannot be seen.
BitField.name: CPULKRF

BitField.name: OPMODE0

BitField.description: Send Channel 0 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 0 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH0SND

BitField.description: Send Channel 1 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 1 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH1SND

BitField.description: Send Channel 2 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 2 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH2SND

BitField.description: Send Channel 3 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 3 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH3SND

BitField.description: Recall Channel 1 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 1 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH0RC

BitField.description: Recall Channel 1 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 1 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH1RC

BitField.description: Recall Channel 2 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 2 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH2RC

BitField.description: Recall Channel 3 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 3 message. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH3RC

BitField.description:
WDT Reset Flag (Read Only)
The WDT reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Watchdog Timer or Window Watchdog Timer to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer register RSTF(WDTx_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer register WWDTRF(WWDTx_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT time-out reset.
BitField.name: WDTRF

BitField.description:
System Reset Flag (Read Only)
The system reset flag is set by the "Reset Signal" from the Cortex-M4 core to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: From Cortex-M4 side, this bit set to 1 cannot be seen.
BitField.name: SYSRF

BitField.description: CPU Reset Flag (Read Only)\nThe CPU reset flag is set by hardware if software writes CPURST (SYS_IPRST0[3:1]) 1 to reset counterpart CPU (any of A35 Core or M4 Core).\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
BitField.name: CPURF

BitField.description:
CPU Lockup Reset Flag (Read Only)
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: When CPU lockup happened under ICE is connected, this flag will set to 1 but chip will not reset.
Note 3: From Cortex-M4 side, this bit set to 1 cannot be seen.
BitField.name: CPULKRF

BitField.description: Operating Mode of Other Side Core 0, Representing A35/M4 Core 0 (Read Only)\nThis bit field indicates the operating mode of the core 0 of the other side.\n
BitField.name: OPMODE0

BitField.description: Operating Mode of Other Side Core 1, Representing A35 Core 1 (Read Only)\nThis bit field indicates the operating mode of the core 1 of the other side.\nNote: This field can only be accessed by Cortex-M4.
BitField.name: OPMODE1

BitField.name: TRGGI1

BitField.description: Trigger General Interrupt 2\nWrite this bit 1 to trigger general interrupt 2.
BitField.name: TRGGI2

BitField.description: Trigger General Interrupt 3\nWrite this bit 1 to trigger general interrupt 3.
BitField.name: TRGGI3

BitField.description: Send Channel 0 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 0 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH0SND

BitField.description: Send Channel 1 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 1 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH1SND

BitField.description: Send Channel 2 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 2 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH2SND

BitField.description: Send Channel 3 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to send TX channel 3 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 1 or not. Otherwise, the receiver may get unpredictable data.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH3SND

BitField.description: Recall Channel 1 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 1 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH0RC

BitField.description: Recall Channel 1 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 1 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH1RC

BitField.description: Recall Channel 2 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 2 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH2RC

BitField.description: Recall Channel 3 Message\nWrite 1 to this bit to recall TX channel 3 message. Before write 1 to this bit, sender should check the corresponding CHxRDY bit in TXSTS is 0 or not.\nNote: Write 0 to this bit has no effect. Write 1 to SND and RC bits of the same channel simultaneously will yield unpredictable result.
BitField.name: CH3RC

BitField.description: Channel 1 Message Ready\nThis bit automatically cleared to 0 after write 1 to CH1SND. Automatically set to 1 after recall complete or receiver notify message read.
BitField.name: CH1RDY

BitField.description: Channel 2 Message Ready\nThis bit automatically cleared to 0 after write 1 to CH2SND. Automatically set to 1 after recall complete or receiver notify message read.

BitField.description: Channel 3 Message Ready\nThis bit automatically cleared to 0 after write 1 to CH3SND. Automatically set to 1 after recall complete or receiver notify message read.

BitField.description: RX Message Channel 0 ACK\nWrite 1 to notify sender that channel 0 message has been read. Write 0 to this bit has no effect.\nWrite 1 will clear CH0RDY.
BitField.name: CH0ACK

BitField.description: RX Message Channel 1 ACK\nWrite 1 to notify sender that channel 1 message has been read. Write 0 to this bit has no effect.\nWrite 1 will clear CH1RDY.
BitField.name: CH1ACK

BitField.description: RX Message Channel 2 ACK\nWrite 1 to notify sender that channel 2 message has been read. Write 0 to this bit has no effect.\nWrite 1 will clear CH2RDY.
BitField.name: CH2ACK

BitField.description: RX Message Channel 3 ACK\nWrite 1 to notify sender that channel 3 message has been read. Write 0 to this bit has no effect.\nWrite 1 will clear CH3RDY.
BitField.name: CH3ACK

BitField.description: RX Channel 0 Message Ready\nNote: This bit is automatically set to 1 after sender writes 1 to CH0SND. It is automatically cleared to 0 after recall complete or write 1 to CH0ACK.
BitField.name: CH0RDY

BitField.description: RX Channel 1 Message Ready\nNote: This bit is automatically set to 1 after sender writes 1 to CH1SND. It is automatically cleared to 0 after recall complete or write 1 to CH1ACK.
BitField.name: CH1RDY

BitField.description: RX Channel 2 Message Ready\nNote: This bit is automatically set to 1 after sender writes 1 to CH2SND. It is automatically cleared to 0 after recall complete or write 1 to CH2ACK.
BitField.name: CH2RDY

BitField.description: RX Channel 3 Message Ready\nNote: This bit is automatically set to 1 after sender writes 1 to CH3SND. It is automatically cleared to 0 after recall complete or write 1 to CH3ACK.
BitField.name: CH3RDY
