BitField.description: Read DQS gating Calibration\nIndicates, if set, that the DATX8 has finished doing period measurement calibration for the read DQS gating LCDL.
BitField.name: GDQSCAL

BitField.description: Write Leveling Calibration\nIndicates, if set, that the DATX8 has finished doing period measurement calibration for the write leveling slave delay line.
BitField.name: WLCAL

BitField.description: Write Leveling Done\nIndicates, if set, that the DATX8 has completed write leveling.
BitField.name: WLDONE

BitField.description: Write Leveling Error\nIndicates, if set, that there is a write leveling error in the DATX8.
BitField.name: WLERR

BitField.description: Write Leveling Period\nReturns the DDR clock period measured by the write leveling LCDL during calibration. The measured period is used to generate the control of the write leveling pipeline which is a function of the write-leveling delay and the clock period. This value is PVT compensated.
BitField.name: WLPRD

BitField.description: DATX8 PLL Lock\nIndicates, if set, that the DATX8 PLL has locked. This is a direct status of the DATX8 PLL lock pin.
BitField.name: DPLOCK

BitField.description: Read DQS gating Period\nReturns the DDR clock period measured by the read DQS gating LCDL during calibration. This value is PVT compensated.
BitField.name: GDQSPRD

BitField.description: DQS Gate Training Error\nIndicates, if set, that there is an error in DQS gate training. One bit for each of the up to 4 ranks.
BitField.name: QSGERR

BitField.description: Write Leveling DQ Status\nCaptures the write leveling DQ status from the DRAM during software write leveling.
BitField.name: WLDQ

Register.description: DATX8 General Status Registers 1 for Byte Lane0
Register.name: DX0GSR1

BitField.description: Delay Line Test Done\nIndicates, if set, that the PHY control block has finished doing period measurement of the DATX8 delay line digital test output.
BitField.name: DLTDONE

BitField.description: Delay Line Test Code\nReturns the code measured by the PHY control block that corresponds to the period of the DATX8 delay line digital test output.
BitField.name: DLTCODE

Register.description: DATX8 General Timing Register for Byte Lane0
Register.name: DX0GTR

BitField.description: Rank n DQS Gating System Latency\nThis is used to increase the number of clock cycles needed to expect valid DDR read data by up to seven extra clock cycles. This is used to compensate for board delays and other system delays. Power-up default is 000 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic DQS data training but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every three bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0DGSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1DGSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values are 0 to 7.
BitField.name: R0DGSL

BitField.description: Rank n DQS Gating System Latency\nThis is used to increase the number of clock cycles needed to expect valid DDR read data by up to seven extra clock cycles. This is used to compensate for board delays and other system delays. Power-up default is 000 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic DQS data training but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every three bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0DGSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1DGSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values are 0 to 7.
BitField.name: R1DGSL

BitField.description: Rank n DQS Gating System Latency\nThis is used to increase the number of clock cycles needed to expect valid DDR read data by up to seven extra clock cycles. This is used to compensate for board delays and other system delays. Power-up default is 000 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic DQS data training but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every three bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0DGSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1DGSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values are 0 to 7.
BitField.name: R2DGSL

BitField.description: Rank n DQS Gating System Latency\nThis is used to increase the number of clock cycles needed to expect valid DDR read data by up to seven extra clock cycles. This is used to compensate for board delays and other system delays. Power-up default is 000 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic DQS data training but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every three bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0DGSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1DGSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values are 0 to 7.
BitField.name: R3DGSL

BitField.description: Rank n Write Leveling System Latency\nThis is used to adjust the write latency after write leveling. Power-up default is 01 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic write leveling but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every two bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0WLSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1WLSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values:\n
BitField.name: R0WLSL

BitField.description: Rank n Write Leveling System Latency\nThis is used to adjust the write latency after write leveling. Power-up default is 01 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic write leveling but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every two bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0WLSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1WLSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values:\n
BitField.name: R1WLSL

BitField.description: Rank n Write Leveling System Latency\nThis is used to adjust the write latency after write leveling. Power-up default is 01 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic write leveling but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every two bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0WLSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1WLSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values:\n
BitField.name: R2WLSL

BitField.description: Rank n Write Leveling System Latency\nThis is used to adjust the write latency after write leveling. Power-up default is 01 (i.e. no extra clock cycles required). The SL fields are initially set by the PUB during automatic write leveling but these values can be overwritten by a direct write to this register. Every two bits of this register control the latency of each of the (up to) four ranks. R0WLSL controls the latency of rank 0, R1WLSL controls rank 1, and so on. Valid values:\n
BitField.name: R3WLSL

Register.description: External Bus Interface Bank0 Control Register
Register.name: EBI_CTL0

BitField.description: EBI Enable Bit\nThis bit is the functional enable bit for EBI.\n
BitField.name: EN

BitField.description: EBI Data Width 16-bit Select\nThis bit defines if the EBI data width is 8-bit or 16-bit.\n
BitField.name: DW16

BitField.description: Chip Select Pin Polar Inverse\nThis bit defines the active level of EBI chip select pin (EBI_nCS).\n
BitField.name: CSPOLINV

BitField.description: EBI Address/Data Bus Separate Mode Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: ADSEPEN

BitField.description: Continuous Data Access Mode\nWhen continuous access mode enabled, the tASU, tALE and tLHD cycles are bypass for continuous data transfer request.\n
BitField.name: CACCESS

BitField.description: External Output Clock Divider\nThe frequency of EBI output clock (MCLK) is controlled by MCLKDIV as follow:\n
BitField.name: MCLKDIV

BitField.description: Extend Time of ALE\nThe EBI_ALE high pulse period (tALE) to latch the address can be controlled by TALE.\nNote: This field only available in EBI_CTL0 register.
BitField.name: TALE

BitField.description: EBI Write Buffer Enable Bit\nNote: This bit only available in EBI_CTL0 register.
BitField.name: WBUFEN

Register.description: External Bus Interface Bank0 Timing Control Register
Register.name: EBI_TCTL0

BitField.description: EBI Data Access Time\nTACC defines data access time (tACC).\n
BitField.name: TACC

BitField.description: EBI Data Access Hold Time\nTAHD defines data access hold time (tAHD).\n
BitField.name: TAHD

BitField.description: Idle Cycle After Write\nThis field defines the number of W2X idle cycle.\nWhen write action is finished, W2X idle cycle is inserted and EBI_nCS return to idle state.
BitField.name: W2X

BitField.description: Access Hold Time Disable Control When Read\n
BitField.name: RAHDOFF

BitField.description: Access Hold Time Disable Control When Write\n
BitField.name: WAHDOFF

BitField.description: Idle Cycle Between Read-to-read\nThis field defines the number of R2R idle cycle.\nWhen read action is finished and the next action is going to read, R2R idle cycle is inserted and EBI_nCS return to idle state.
BitField.name: R2R

BitField.description: Port A-N Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit\nThe DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (Px_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (Px_DBCTL [3:0]).\nThe de-bounce function is valid only for edge triggered interrupt. If the interrupt mode is level triggered, the de-bounce enable bit is ignored.
BitField.name: DBEN0

BitField.description:
Port A-N Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.
If the pin is set as the level trigger interrupt, only one level can be set on the registers RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16])/FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]). If both levels to trigger interrupt are set, the setting is ignored and no interrupt will occur.
The de-bounce function is valid only for edge triggered interrupt. If the interrupt mode is level triggered, the de-bounce enable bit is ignored.

Port A-N Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.

If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Port A-N Pin[n] Rising Edge or High Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function. 
When setting the RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at high level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from low to high.

Register.description: PA Pull-up and Pull-down Selection Register
Register.name: PA_PUSEL

BitField.description:
Port A-N Pin[n] Pull-up and Pull-down Enable Register
Determine each I/O Pull-up/pull-down of Px.n pins.
Note: 
Basically, the pull-up control and pull-down control has following behavior limitation.
The independent pull-up control register only valid when MODEn is set as input and open-drain mode even if I/O function is switched to multi-function pin, e.g. UARTx_RXD.
The independent pull-down control register is only valid when MODEn set as tri-state mode.
When both pull-up pull-down is set as 1 at "tri-state" mode, keep I/O in tri-state mode.

Register.description: GPIO PA.n Pin Data Input/Output Register
Register.name: PA0_PDIO

BitField.description:
GPIO Px.n Pin Data Input/Output
Writing this bit can control one GPIO pin output value.
Read this register to get GPIO pin status.
For example, writing PA0_PDIO will reflect the written value to bit DOUT (Px_DOUT[0]), reading PA0_PDIO will return the value of PIN (PA_PIN[0]).
Note: The writing operation will not be affected by register DATMSK (Px_DATMSK[n]).
BitField.name: PDIO

Register.description: Descriptor Table Control Register of PDMA Channel n
Register.name: PDMAx_DSCT0_CTL

BitField.description: PDMA Operation Mode Selection\nNote: Before filling new transfer task in the Descriptor Table, user must check the PDMA_INTSTS[1] to make sure the current task is complete.
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Transfer Type\n
BitField.name: TXTYPE

BitField.description: Burst Size\nThis field is used for peripheral to determine the burst size or used for determine the re-arbitration size.\nNote: This field is only useful in burst transfer type.
BitField.name: BURSIZE

BitField.description: Table Interrupt Disable Bit\nThis field can be used to decide whether to enable table interrupt or not. If the TBINTDIS bit is enabled it will not generates TDIFn(PDMA_TDSTS[7:0]) when PDMA controller finishes transfer task.\nNote: This function is only for Scatter-gather mode.
BitField.name: TBINTDIS

BitField.description: Destination Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the destination address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: DAINC

BitField.description: Transfer Width Selection\nThis field is used for transfer width.\nNote: The PDMA transfer source address (PDMA_DSCTn_SA) and PDMA transfer destination address (PDMA_DSCTn_DA) should be alignment under the TXWIDTH selection
BitField.name: TXWIDTH

BitField.description: Stride Mode Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: STRIDEEN

BitField.description: Transfer Count\nThe TXCNT represents the required number of PDMA transfer, the real transfer count is (TXCNT + 1); the maximum transfer count is 65536, every transfer may be byte, half-word or word that is dependent on TXWIDTH field.\nNote: When PDMA finishes each transfer data, this field will be decreased immediately.
BitField.name: TXCNT

BitField.description:
PDMA Next Descriptor Table Offset
This field indicates the offset of the next descriptor table address in system memory. 
Read Operation:
When operating in Scatter-gather mode, the last two bits NEXT[1:0] will become reserved, and indicate the first next address of system memory.
Note 1: The descriptor table address must be word boundary.
Note 2: Before filling transfer task in the descriptor table, user must check if the descriptor table is complete.
BitField.name: NEXT

BitField.description:
Channel 0 Request Source Selection
This filed defines which peripheral is connected to PDMA channel 0. User can configure the peripheral by setting REQSRC0.
Note 1: A peripheral cannot be assigned to two channels at the same time.
Note 2: This field is useless when transfer between memory and memory.
BitField.name: REQSRC0

Register.name: PDMAx_DSCT0_CTL

BitField.description: PDMA Operation Mode Selection\nNote: Before filling new transfer task in the Descriptor Table, user must check the PDMA_INTSTS[1] to make sure the current task is complete.
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Transfer Type\n
BitField.name: TXTYPE

BitField.description: Burst Size\nThis field is used for peripheral to determine the burst size or used for determine the re-arbitration size.\nNote: This field is only useful in burst transfer type.
BitField.name: BURSIZE

BitField.description: Table Interrupt Disable Bit\nThis field can be used to decide whether to enable table interrupt or not. If the TBINTDIS bit is enabled it will not generates TDIFn(PDMA_TDSTS[7:0]) when PDMA controller finishes transfer task.\nNote: This function is only for Scatter-gather mode.
BitField.name: TBINTDIS

BitField.description: Source Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the source address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: SAINC

BitField.description: Destination Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the destination address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: DAINC

BitField.description: Transfer Width Selection\nThis field is used for transfer width.\nNote: The PDMA transfer source address (PDMA_DSCTn_SA) and PDMA transfer destination address (PDMA_DSCTn_DA) should be alignment under the TXWIDTH selection
BitField.name: TXWIDTH

BitField.description: Stride Mode Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: STRIDEEN

BitField.description: Transfer Count\nThe TXCNT represents the required number of PDMA transfer, the real transfer count is (TXCNT + 1); the maximum transfer count is 65536, every transfer may be byte, half-word or word that is dependent on TXWIDTH field.\nNote: When PDMA finishes each transfer data, this field will be decreased immediately.
BitField.name: TXCNT

BitField.description:
PDMA Next Descriptor Table Offset
This field indicates the offset of the next descriptor table address in system memory. 
Read Operation:
When operating in Scatter-gather mode, the last two bits NEXT[1:0] will become reserved, and indicate the first next address of system memory.
Note 1: The descriptor table address must be word boundary.
Note 2: Before filling transfer task in the descriptor table, user must check if the descriptor table is complete.
BitField.name: NEXT

BitField.description: PDMA Execution Next Descriptor Table Offset\nThis field indicates the offset of next descriptor table address of current execution descriptor table in system memory. \nNote: Write operation is useless in this field.
BitField.name: EXENEXT

BitField.description:
PDMA Software Request (Write Only)
Set this bit to 1 to generate a software request to PDMA [n].
Note 1: User can read PDMA_TRGSTS register to know which channel is on active. Active flag may be triggered by software request or peripheral request.
Note 2: If user does not enable corresponding PDMA channel, the software request will be ignored.

BitField.description: PDMA Channel Request Status (Read Only)\nThis flag indicates whether channel[n] have a request or not, no matter request from software or peripheral. When the PDMA controller finishes channel transfer, this bit will be cleared automatically. \nNote: If user pauses or resets each PDMA transfer by setting PDMA_PAUSE or PDMA_CHRST register respectively, this bit will be cleared automatically after finishing the current transfer.

BitField.description:

Note 2: User can write 1 to clear this bit.

BitField.description:
Channel 0 Request Source Selection
This filed defines which peripheral is connected to PDMA channel 0. User can configure the peripheral by setting REQSRC0.
Note 1: A peripheral cannot be assigned to two channels at the same time.
Note 2: This field is useless when transfer between memory and memory.
BitField.name: REQSRC0

BitField.description: PDMA Operation Mode Selection\nNote: Before filling new transfer task in the Descriptor Table, user must check the PDMA_INTSTS[1] to make sure the current task is complete.
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Transfer Type\n
BitField.name: TXTYPE

BitField.description: Burst Size\nThis field is used for peripheral to determine the burst size or used for determine the re-arbitration size.\nNote: This field is only useful in burst transfer type.
BitField.name: BURSIZE

BitField.description: Table Interrupt Disable Bit\nThis field can be used to decide whether to enable table interrupt or not. If the TBINTDIS bit is enabled it will not generates TDIFn(PDMA_TDSTS[7:0]) when PDMA controller finishes transfer task.\nNote: This function is only for Scatter-gather mode.
BitField.name: TBINTDIS

BitField.description: Source Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the source address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: SAINC

BitField.description: Destination Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the destination address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: DAINC

BitField.description: Transfer Width Selection\nThis field is used for transfer width.\nNote: The PDMA transfer source address (PDMA_DSCTn_SA) and PDMA transfer destination address (PDMA_DSCTn_DA) should be alignment under the TXWIDTH selection
BitField.name: TXWIDTH

BitField.description: Stride Mode Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: STRIDEEN

BitField.description: Transfer Count\nThe TXCNT represents the required number of PDMA transfer, the real transfer count is (TXCNT + 1); the maximum transfer count is 65536, every transfer may be byte, half-word or word that is dependent on TXWIDTH field.\nNote: When PDMA finishes each transfer data, this field will be decreased immediately.
BitField.name: TXCNT

BitField.description:
PDMA Next Descriptor Table Offset
This field indicates the offset of the next descriptor table address in system memory. 
Read Operation:
When operating in Scatter-gather mode, the last two bits NEXT[1:0] will become reserved, and indicate the first next address of system memory.
Note 1: The descriptor table address must be word boundary.
Note 2: Before filling transfer task in the descriptor table, user must check if the descriptor table is complete.
BitField.name: NEXT

BitField.description: PDMA Execution Next Descriptor Table Offset\nThis field indicates the offset of next descriptor table address of current execution descriptor table in system memory. \nNote: Write operation is useless in this field.
BitField.name: EXENEXT

BitField.description:
PDMA Software Request (Write Only)
Set this bit to 1 to generate a software request to PDMA [n].
Note 1: User can read PDMA_TRGSTS register to know which channel is on active. Active flag may be triggered by software request or peripheral request.
Note 2: If user does not enable corresponding PDMA channel, the software request will be ignored.

BitField.description:
PDMA Software Request (Write Only)
Set this bit to 1 to generate a software request to PDMA [n].
Note 1: User can read PDMA_TRGSTS register to know which channel is on active. Active flag may be triggered by software request or peripheral request.
Note 2: If user does not enable corresponding PDMA channel, the software request will be ignored.
BitField.name: SWREQ1

BitField.description: PDMA Channel Request Status (Read Only)\nThis flag indicates whether channel[n] have a request or not, no matter request from software or peripheral. When the PDMA controller finishes channel transfer, this bit will be cleared automatically. \nNote: If user pauses or resets each PDMA transfer by setting PDMA_PAUSE or PDMA_CHRST register respectively, this bit will be cleared automatically after finishing the current transfer.
BitField.name: REQSTS0

Register.description: PDMA Time-out Counter Ch1 and Ch0 Register
Register.name: PDMAx_TOC0_1

BitField.description: Time-out Counter for Channel 0\nThis controls the period of time-out function for channel 0. The calculation unit is based on TOUTPSC0 (PDMA_TOUTPSC[2:0]) clock.\n
BitField.name: TOC0

BitField.description: Time-out Counter for Channel 1\nThis controls the period of time-out function for channel 1. The calculation unit is based on TOUTPSC1 (PDMA_TOUTPSC[6:4]) clock. The example of time-out period can refer TOC0 bit description.
BitField.name: TOC1

Register.description: PDMA Time-out Counter Ch3 and Ch2 Register
Register.name: PDMAx_TOC2_3

BitField.description:
Channel 0 Request Source Selection
This filed defines which peripheral is connected to PDMA channel 0. User can configure the peripheral by setting REQSRC0.
Note 1: A peripheral cannot be assigned to two channels at the same time.

BitField.description: PDMA Operation Mode Selection\nNote: Before filling new transfer task in the Descriptor Table, user must check the PDMA_INTSTS[1] to make sure the current task is complete.
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Transfer Type\n
BitField.name: TXTYPE

BitField.description: Burst Size\nThis field is used for peripheral to determine the burst size or used for determine the re-arbitration size.\nNote: This field is only useful in burst transfer type.
BitField.name: BURSIZE

BitField.description: Table Interrupt Disable Bit\nThis field can be used to decide whether to enable table interrupt or not. If the TBINTDIS bit is enabled it will not generates TDIFn(PDMA_TDSTS[7:0]) when PDMA controller finishes transfer task.\nNote: This function is only for Scatter-gather mode.
BitField.name: TBINTDIS

BitField.description: Source Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the source address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: SAINC

BitField.description: Destination Address Increment\nThis field is used to set the destination address increment size.\nNote: The fixed address function does not support in memory to memory transfer type.
BitField.name: DAINC

BitField.description: Transfer Width Selection\nThis field is used for transfer width.\nNote: The PDMA transfer source address (PDMA_DSCTn_SA) and PDMA transfer destination address (PDMA_DSCTn_DA) should be alignment under the TXWIDTH selection
BitField.name: TXWIDTH

BitField.description: Stride Mode Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: STRIDEEN

BitField.description: Transfer Count\nThe TXCNT represents the required number of PDMA transfer, the real transfer count is (TXCNT + 1); the maximum transfer count is 65536, every transfer may be byte, half-word or word that is dependent on TXWIDTH field.\nNote: When PDMA finishes each transfer data, this field will be decreased immediately.
BitField.name: TXCNT

BitField.description:
PDMA Next Descriptor Table Offset
This field indicates the offset of the next descriptor table address in system memory. 
Read Operation:
When operating in Scatter-gather mode, the last two bits NEXT[1:0] will become reserved, and indicate the first next address of system memory.
Note 1: The descriptor table address must be word boundary.
Note 2: Before filling transfer task in the descriptor table, user must check if the descriptor table is complete.
BitField.name: NEXT

BitField.description: PDMA Execution Next Descriptor Table Offset\nThis field indicates the offset of next descriptor table address of current execution descriptor table in system memory. \nNote: Write operation is useless in this field.
BitField.name: EXENEXT

BitField.description:
PDMA Software Request (Write Only)
Set this bit to 1 to generate a software request to PDMA [n].
Note 1: User can read PDMA_TRGSTS register to know which channel is on active. Active flag may be triggered by software request or peripheral request.
Note 2: If user does not enable corresponding PDMA channel, the software request will be ignored.

BitField.description: PDMA Channel Request Status (Read Only)\nThis flag indicates whether channel[n] have a request or not, no matter request from software or peripheral. When the PDMA controller finishes channel transfer, this bit will be cleared automatically. \nNote: If user pauses or resets each PDMA transfer by setting PDMA_PAUSE or PDMA_CHRST register respectively, this bit will be cleared automatically after finishing the current transfer.
BitField.name: REQSTS0

BitField.description:
Channel 0 Request Source Selection
This filed defines which peripheral is connected to PDMA channel 0. User can configure the peripheral by setting REQSRC0.
Note 1: A peripheral cannot be assigned to two channels at the same time.
Note 2: This field is useless when transfer between memory and memory.
BitField.name: REQSRC0

BitField.description:
Inter-timer Trigger Mode Enable Bit
Setting this bit will enable the inter-timer trigger capture function.
The Timer0/2/4/6/8/10 will be in event counter mode and counting with external clock source or event.Also, Timer1/3/5/7/9/11 will be in trigger-counting mode of capture function.
Note: For Timer1/3/5/7/9/11, this bit is ignored and the read back value is always 0.
BitField.name: INTRGEN

BitField.description: Periodic Mode Behavior Selection Enable Bit\nIf updated CMPDAT value < CNT, CNT will be reset to default value.

BitField.name: TGLPINSEL

BitField.name: CAPSRC

BitField.description: Wake-up Function Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, while timer interrupt flag TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0]) is 1 and INTEN (TIMERx_CTL[29]) is enabled, the timer interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to CPU.\n
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Event Counter Mode Enable Bit \nThis bit is for external counting pin function enabled. \nNote: When timer is used as an event counter, this bit should be set to 1 and select PCLK as timer clock source.
BitField.name: EXTCNTEN

BitField.description: Timer Active Status Bit (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates the 24-bit up counter status.\nNote: This bit may active when CNT 0 transition to CNT 1.
BitField.name: ACTSTS

BitField.description: Timer Counting Mode Select\n
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, when the timer time-out interrupt flag TIF is set to 1, the timer interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Timer Counting Enable Bit\nNote 3: Set enable/disable this bit needs 2 * TMR_CLK period to become active, user can read ACTSTS (TIMERx_CTL[25]) to check enable/disable command is completed or not.
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nTIMER counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of Timer while 24-bit timer up counter CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) value reaches to CMPDAT (TIMERx_CMP[23:0]) value.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TIF

BitField.description: Timer Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of timer.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TWKF

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register
Read operation.
Read this register to get CNT value. For example:
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 0, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit counter value.
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 1, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit event input counter value.
Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register Reset Active (Read Only)
This bit indicates if the counter reset operation active.
When user writes this CNT register, timer starts to reset its internal 24-bit timer up-counter to 0 and reload 8-bit pre-scale counter. At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.
BitField.name: RSTACT

BitField.description: Timer Capture Data Register\nWhen CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, CAPFUNCS (TIMERx_EXTCTL[4]) bit is 0, and a transition on TMx_EXT pin matched the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, CAPIF (TIMERx_EINTSTS[0]) will set to 1 and the current timer counter value CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be auto-loaded into this CAPDAT field.
BitField.name: CAPDAT

BitField.description: Timer External Count Phase \n
BitField.name: CNTPHASE

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Pin Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the TMx_EXT capture pin input function.\n
BitField.name: CAPEN

BitField.description: Capture Function Selection\n
BitField.name: CAPFUNCS

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Interrupt Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: CAPIEN

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Pin De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx_EXT pin is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CAPDBEN

BitField.description: Timer Counter Pin De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx pin is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CNTDBEN

BitField.description: Internal Capture Source Selection\nNote: these bits only available when CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) is 1.
BitField.name: ICAPSSEL

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Pin Edge Detect\nWhen first capture event is generated, the CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be reset to 0 and first CAPDAT (TIMERx_CAP[23:0]) should be to 0.\n
BitField.name: CAPEDGE

BitField.name: ECNTSSEL

BitField.description: Timer Capture Source Divider\nThis bits indicate the divide scale for capture source.\nNote: Sets ICAPSSEL (TIMERx_EXTCTL[10:8]) and CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) to select capture source.
BitField.name: CAPSDIV

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the timer external capture interrupt flag status.\nNote 3: There is a new incoming capture event detected before CPU clearing the CAPIF status. If the above condition occurred, the Timer will keep register TIMERx_CAP unchanged and drop the new capture value.
BitField.name: CAPIF

BitField.description: Trigger Source Select Bit\nThis bit is used to select internal trigger source is form timer time-out interrupt signal or capture interrupt signal.\n
BitField.name: TRGSSEL

BitField.description: Trigger EPWM and BPWM Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be as EPWM and BPWM counter clock source.\n
BitField.name: TRGPWM

BitField.description: Trigger EADC Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered EADC conversion.\n
BitField.name: TRGEADC

BitField.description: Trigger PDMA Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered PDMA transfer.\n
BitField.name: TRGPDMA

BitField.description: Function Selection\nNote: When timer is used as PWM, the clock source of time controller will be forced to PCLKx automatically.
BitField.name: FUNCSEL

BitField.name: CNTTYPE

BitField.name: CNTMODE

BitField.description: Center Re-load\nIn up-down count type, PERIOD will load to PBUF when current PWM period is completed always and CMP will load to CMPBUF at the center point of current period.

BitField.description: Immediately Load Enable Bit\nNote: If IMMLDEN is enabled, CTRLD will be invalid.
BitField.name: IMMLDEN

BitField.description: PWM Output Mode\nThis bit controls the output mode of corresponding PWM channel.\n

BitField.description:
PWM Period Register
In up count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
In down count type: PWM counter counts from PERIOD to 0, and restarts from PERIOD.
In up-down count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, then decrements to 0 and repeats again.
In up and down count type:
Note: User should take care DIRF (TIMERx_PWMCNT[16]) bit in up/down/up-down count type to monitor current counter direction in each count type.
BitField.name: PERIOD

Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register

PWM Compare Down Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in down count direction and reaches CMP.

Setting this bit will enable the inter-timer trigger capture function.
The Timer0/2/4/6/8/10 will be in event counter mode and counting with external clock source or event.Also, Timer1/3/5/7/9/11 will be in trigger-counting mode of capture function.
Note: For Timer1/3/5/7/9/11, this bit is ignored and the read back value is always 0.

BitField.description: Event Counter Mode Enable Bit \nThis bit is for external counting pin function enabled. \nNote: When timer is used as an event counter, this bit should be set to 1 and select PCLK as timer clock source.

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nTIMER counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of Timer while 24-bit timer up counter CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) value reaches to CMPDAT (TIMERx_CMP[23:0]) value.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TIF

BitField.description: Timer Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of timer.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TWKF

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register
Read operation.
Read this register to get CNT value. For example:
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 0, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit counter value.
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 1, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit event input counter value.
Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register Reset Active (Read Only)
This bit indicates if the counter reset operation active.
When user writes this CNT register, timer starts to reset its internal 24-bit timer up-counter to 0 and reload 8-bit pre-scale counter. At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.
BitField.name: RSTACT

BitField.description: Timer Capture Data Register\nWhen CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, CAPFUNCS (TIMERx_EXTCTL[4]) bit is 0, and a transition on TMx_EXT pin matched the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, CAPIF (TIMERx_EINTSTS[0]) will set to 1 and the current timer counter value CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be auto-loaded into this CAPDAT field.

At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.

Note: User should take care DIRF (TIMERx_PWMCNT[16]) bit in up/down/up-down count type to monitor current counter direction in each count type.

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.

Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.

BitField.description: Clear PWM Counter Control Bit\nIt is automatically cleared by hardware.\n

BitField.description:
PWM Period Register

In down count type: PWM counter counts from PERIOD to 0, and restarts from PERIOD.
In up-down count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, then decrements to 0 and repeats again.
In up and down count type:
Note: User should take care DIRF (TIMERx_PWMCNT[16]) bit in up/down/up-down count type to monitor current counter direction in each count type.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description:
PWM Period Point Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches PERIOD.
Note 1: In up-down count type, PIF flag means the center point flag of current PWM period.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: PIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Up Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in up count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPUIF flag in up count type and up-down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPUIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Down Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in down count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPDIF flag in down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPDIF

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKEIF0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKLIF0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKLIF1

BitField.description: Edge -detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF0 1 to clear BRKEIF0 flag and PWMx_CH0 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF1 1 to clear BRKEIF1 flag and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS1

BitField.description:
Inter-timer Trigger Mode Enable Bit
Setting this bit will enable the inter-timer trigger capture function.
The Timer0/2/4/6/8/10 will be in event counter mode and counting with external clock source or event.Also, Timer1/3/5/7/9/11 will be in trigger-counting mode of capture function.
Note: For Timer1/3/5/7/9/11, this bit is ignored and the read back value is always 0.

BitField.description: Capture Pin Source Selection\n
BitField.name: CAPSRC

BitField.description: Wake-up Function Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, while timer interrupt flag TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0]) is 1 and INTEN (TIMERx_CTL[29]) is enabled, the timer interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to CPU.\n
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Event Counter Mode Enable Bit \nThis bit is for external counting pin function enabled. \nNote: When timer is used as an event counter, this bit should be set to 1 and select PCLK as timer clock source.
BitField.name: EXTCNTEN

BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Timer Counting Enable Bit\nNote 3: Set enable/disable this bit needs 2 * TMR_CLK period to become active, user can read ACTSTS (TIMERx_CTL[25]) to check enable/disable command is completed or not.
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nTIMER counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of Timer while 24-bit timer up counter CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) value reaches to CMPDAT (TIMERx_CMP[23:0]) value.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TIF

BitField.description: Timer Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of timer.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TWKF

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register
Read operation.
Read this register to get CNT value. For example:
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 0, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit counter value.
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 1, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit event input counter value.
Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register Reset Active (Read Only)
This bit indicates if the counter reset operation active.
When user writes this CNT register, timer starts to reset its internal 24-bit timer up-counter to 0 and reload 8-bit pre-scale counter. At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.
BitField.name: RSTACT

BitField.description: Timer Capture Data Register\nWhen CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, CAPFUNCS (TIMERx_EXTCTL[4]) bit is 0, and a transition on TMx_EXT pin matched the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, CAPIF (TIMERx_EINTSTS[0]) will set to 1 and the current timer counter value CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be auto-loaded into this CAPDAT field.
BitField.name: CAPDAT

BitField.description: PWM Zero Point Interrupt Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches 0.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.

BitField.description:
PWM Period Point Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches PERIOD.
Note 1: In up-down count type, PIF flag means the center point flag of current PWM period.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: PIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Up Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in up count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPUIF flag in up count type and up-down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPUIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Down Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in down count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPDIF flag in down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPDIF

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKEIF0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKEIF1

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKLIF0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: BRKLIF1

BitField.description: Edge -detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF0 1 to clear BRKEIF0 flag and PWMx_CH0 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF1 1 to clear BRKEIF1 flag and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS1

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS1

BitField.name: SYNCSRC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Synchronous Trigger Enable Bit (Write Only)\nPMW counter synchronous function is used to make selected PWM channels (include TIMER0/1/2/3 PWM, TIMER0/1 PWM and TIMER2/3 PWM) start counting or clear counter at the same time according to TIMERx_PWMSCTL setting.\nNote: This bit is only available in TIMER0 and TIMER2.

BitField.description: Prescale Counter\nNote: Update prescale counter value will reset internal 8-bit prescale counter and 24-bit up counter value.
BitField.name: PSC

BitField.description:
Inter-timer Trigger Mode Enable Bit
Setting this bit will enable the inter-timer trigger capture function.
The Timer0/2/4/6/8/10 will be in event counter mode and counting with external clock source or event.Also, Timer1/3/5/7/9/11 will be in trigger-counting mode of capture function.
Note: For Timer1/3/5/7/9/11, this bit is ignored and the read back value is always 0.
BitField.name: INTRGEN

BitField.description: Periodic Mode Behavior Selection Enable Bit\nIf updated CMPDAT value < CNT, CNT will be reset to default value.
BitField.name: PERIOSEL

BitField.description: Toggle-output Pin Select\n
BitField.name: TGLPINSEL

BitField.description: Capture Pin Source Selection\n
BitField.name: CAPSRC

BitField.description: Wake-up Function Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, while timer interrupt flag TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0]) is 1 and INTEN (TIMERx_CTL[29]) is enabled, the timer interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to CPU.\n
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Event Counter Mode Enable Bit \nThis bit is for external counting pin function enabled. \nNote: When timer is used as an event counter, this bit should be set to 1 and select PCLK as timer clock source.
BitField.name: EXTCNTEN

BitField.description: Timer Active Status Bit (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates the 24-bit up counter status.\nNote: This bit may active when CNT 0 transition to CNT 1.
BitField.name: ACTSTS

BitField.description: Timer Counting Mode Select\n
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, when the timer time-out interrupt flag TIF is set to 1, the timer interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Timer Counting Enable Bit\nNote 3: Set enable/disable this bit needs 2 * TMR_CLK period to become active, user can read ACTSTS (TIMERx_CTL[25]) to check enable/disable command is completed or not.
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nTIMER counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of Timer while 24-bit timer up counter CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) value reaches to CMPDAT (TIMERx_CMP[23:0]) value.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TIF

BitField.description: Timer Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of timer.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TWKF

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register
Read operation.
Read this register to get CNT value. For example:
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 0, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit counter value.
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 1, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit event input counter value.
Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register Reset Active (Read Only)
This bit indicates if the counter reset operation active.
When user writes this CNT register, timer starts to reset its internal 24-bit timer up-counter to 0 and reload 8-bit pre-scale counter. At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.
BitField.name: RSTACT

BitField.description: Timer Capture Data Register\nWhen CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, CAPFUNCS (TIMERx_EXTCTL[4]) bit is 0, and a transition on TMx_EXT pin matched the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, CAPIF (TIMERx_EINTSTS[0]) will set to 1 and the current timer counter value CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be auto-loaded into this CAPDAT field.
BitField.name: CAPDAT

BitField.description: Timer External Count Phase \n
BitField.name: CNTPHASE

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Pin Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the TMx_EXT capture pin input function.\n
BitField.name: CAPEN

BitField.description: Capture Function Selection\n
BitField.name: CAPFUNCS

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Interrupt Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: CAPIEN

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Pin De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx_EXT pin is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CAPDBEN

BitField.description: Timer Counter Pin De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx pin is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CNTDBEN

BitField.description: Internal Capture Source Selection\nNote: these bits only available when CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) is 1.
BitField.name: ICAPSSEL

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Pin Edge Detect\nWhen first capture event is generated, the CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be reset to 0 and first CAPDAT (TIMERx_CAP[23:0]) should be to 0.\n
BitField.name: CAPEDGE

BitField.description: Event Counter Source Selection to Trigger Event Counter Function\n
BitField.name: ECNTSSEL

BitField.description: Timer Capture Source Divider\nThis bits indicate the divide scale for capture source.\nNote: Sets ICAPSSEL (TIMERx_EXTCTL[10:8]) and CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) to select capture source.
BitField.name: CAPSDIV

BitField.description: Timer External Capture Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the timer external capture interrupt flag status.\nNote 3: There is a new incoming capture event detected before CPU clearing the CAPIF status. If the above condition occurred, the Timer will keep register TIMERx_CAP unchanged and drop the new capture value.
BitField.name: CAPIF

BitField.description: Trigger Source Select Bit\nThis bit is used to select internal trigger source is form timer time-out interrupt signal or capture interrupt signal.\n
BitField.name: TRGSSEL

BitField.description: Trigger EPWM and BPWM Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be as EPWM and BPWM counter clock source.\n
BitField.name: TRGPWM

BitField.description: Trigger EADC Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered EADC conversion.\n
BitField.name: TRGEADC

BitField.description: Trigger PDMA Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered PDMA transfer.\n
BitField.name: TRGPDMA

BitField.description: Function Selection\nNote: When timer is used as PWM, the clock source of time controller will be forced to PCLKx automatically.
BitField.name: FUNCSEL

BitField.description: PWM Counter Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: PWM Counter Behavior Type\n
BitField.name: CNTTYPE

BitField.description: PWM Counter Mode\n
BitField.name: CNTMODE

BitField.description: Center Re-load\nIn up-down count type, PERIOD will load to PBUF when current PWM period is completed always and CMP will load to CMPBUF at the center point of current period.
BitField.name: CTRLD

BitField.description: Immediately Load Enable Bit\nNote: If IMMLDEN is enabled, CTRLD will be invalid.
BitField.name: IMMLDEN

BitField.description: PWM Output Mode\nThis bit controls the output mode of corresponding PWM channel.\n
BitField.name: OUTMODE

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Counter Halt (Write Protect)\nIf debug mode counter halt is enabled, PWM counter will keep current value until exit ICE debug mode. \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_RLKTZS or SYS_RLKTZND or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: DBGHALT

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nPWM output pin will keep output no matter ICE debug mode acknowledged or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: DBGTRIOFF

Register.description: Timer8 PWM Counter Clock Source Register
Register.name: TIMER8_PWMCLKSRC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Clock Source Select\nThe PWM counter clock source can be selected from TMRx_CLK or internal timer time-out or capture event.\nNote: If TIMER0 PWM function is enabled, the PWM counter clock source can be selected from TMR0_CLK, TIMER1 interrupt events, TIMER2 interrupt events, or TIMER3 interrupt events.
BitField.name: CLKSRC

Register.description: Timer8 PWM Counter Clock Pre-scale Register
Register.name: TIMER8_PWMCLKPSC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Clock Pre-scale \nThe active clock of PWM counter is decided by counter clock prescale and divided by (CLKPSC + 1). If CLKPSC is 0, then there is no scaling in PWM counter clock source.
BitField.name: CLKPSC

BitField.description: Clear PWM Counter Control Bit\nIt is automatically cleared by hardware.\n
BitField.name: CNTCLR

BitField.description:
PWM Period Register
In up count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
In down count type: PWM counter counts from PERIOD to 0, and restarts from PERIOD.
In up-down count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, then decrements to 0 and repeats again.
In up and down count type:
Note: User should take care DIRF (TIMERx_PWMCNT[16]) bit in up/down/up-down count type to monitor current counter direction in each count type.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description: PWM Comparator Register\nPWM CMP is used to compare with PWM CNT to generate PWM output waveform, interrupt events and trigger ADC to start conversion.
BitField.name: CMP

BitField.description: Dead-time Counter (Write Protect)\nThe dead-time can be calculated from the following two formulas: \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: DTCNT

BitField.description: Enable Dead-time Insertion for PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nDead-time insertion function is only active when PWM complementary mode is enabled. If dead- time insertion is inactive, the outputs of PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 are complementary without any delay.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: DTEN

BitField.name: DTCKSEL

BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description:
PWM Period Point Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches PERIOD.
Note 1: In up-down count type, PIF flag means the center point flag of current PWM period.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: PIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Up Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in up count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPUIF flag in up count type and up-down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPUIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Down Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in down count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPDIF flag in down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPDIF

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF1 1 to clear BRKEIF1 flag and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.

BitField.description:
EPWM Period Register
Up-Count mode: 
In this mode, EPWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description:
EPWM Comparator Register
CMP is used to compare with CNT (EPWM_CNTn[15:0]) bits to generate EPWM waveform, interrupt and trigger EADC.
In independent mode, CMPDAT0~5 is denoted as 6 independent EPWM_CH0~5 compared point.
In complementary mode, CMPDAT0, 2, 4 is denoted as the first compared point, and CMPDAT1, 3, 5 is denoted as the second compared point for the corresponding 3 complementary pairs EPWM_CH0 and EPWM_CH1, EPWM_CH2 and EPWM_CH3, EPWM_CH4 and EPWM_CH5.
BitField.name: CMP

BitField.description:
Transition Mask Counter
The fault detect result will be masked before counter count from 0 to TRMSKCNT.
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Mask time is EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT +2)
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Mask time EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT +2)

Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSC) is 0:
BitField.name: TRMSKCNT

BitField.description: Fault Detect Mask Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: FDMSKEN

BitField.description:
Deglitch Sampling Cycle
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSC) is 0:
BitField.name: DGSMPCYC

BitField.description:
EPWM Period Register
Up-Count mode: 
In this mode, EPWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description:
EPWM Comparator Register
CMP is used to compare with CNT (EPWM_CNTn[15:0]) bits to generate EPWM waveform, interrupt and trigger EADC.
In independent mode, CMPDAT0~5 is denoted as 6 independent EPWM_CH0~5 compared point.
In complementary mode, CMPDAT0, 2, 4 is denoted as the first compared point, and CMPDAT1, 3, 5 is denoted as the second compared point for the corresponding 3 complementary pairs EPWM_CH0 and EPWM_CH1, EPWM_CH2 and EPWM_CH3, EPWM_CH4 and EPWM_CH5.
BitField.name: CMP

BitField.description:
Transition Mask Counter
The fault detect result will be masked before counter count from 0 to TRMSKCNT.
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Mask time is EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT +2)
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Mask time EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT +2)

Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSC) is 0:
BitField.name: TRMSKCNT

BitField.description: Fault Detect Mask Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: FDMSKEN

BitField.description:
Deglitch Sampling Cycle
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSC) is 0:
BitField.name: DGSMPCYC

BitField.description:
EPWM Period Register
Up-Count mode: 
In this mode, EPWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description:
EPWM Comparator Register
CMP is used to compare with CNT (EPWM_CNTn[15:0]) bits to generate EPWM waveform, interrupt and trigger EADC.
In independent mode, CMPDAT0~5 is denoted as 6 independent EPWM_CH0~5 compared point.
In complementary mode, CMPDAT0, 2, 4 is denoted as the first compared point, and CMPDAT1, 3, 5 is denoted as the second compared point for the corresponding 3 complementary pairs EPWM_CH0 and EPWM_CH1, EPWM_CH2 and EPWM_CH3, EPWM_CH4 and EPWM_CH5.
BitField.name: CMP

BitField.description:
Transition Mask Counter
The fault detect result will be masked before counter count from 0 to TRMSKCNT.
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Mask time is EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT +2)
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Mask time EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT +2)

Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSC) is 0:
BitField.name: TRMSKCNT

BitField.description: Fault Detect Mask Enable Bit\n
BitField.name: FDMSKEN

BitField.description:
Deglitch Sampling Cycle
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSC) is 0:
BitField.name: DGSMPCYC

BitField.description: Input Capture Channel 1 Triggered Flag\nWhen the input capture channel 1 detects a valid edge change at CAP1 input, it will set flag CAPTF1 to high. \nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.

BitField.description: Input Capture Channel 2 Triggered Flag\nWhen the input capture channel 2 detects a valid edge change at CAP2 input, it will set flag CAPTF2 to high. \nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CAPTF2

BitField.description: Input Capture Compare-match Flag\nIf the input capture compare function is enabled, the flag is set by hardware when capture counter (ECAP_CNT) up counts and reaches the ECAP_CNTCMP value.\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CAPCMPF

BitField.description: Input Capture Counter Overflow Flag\nFlag is set by hardware when counter (ECAP_CNT) overflows from 0x00FF_FFFF to zero.\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.

BitField.description: Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter \nA 32-bit up/down counter. When an effective phase pulse is detected, this counter is increased by one if the bit DIRF (QEI_STATUS[8]) is 1 or decreased by one if the bit DIRF(QEI_STATUS[8]) is 0. This register performs an integrator that counts the value proportional to the encoder position. The pulse counter may be initialized to a predetermined value by one of three events occurs:\n
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description: Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter Hold\nWhen the bit HOLDCNT (QEI_CTL[24]) goes from low to high, the CNT(QEI_CNT[31:0]) is copied into CNTHOLD (QEI_CNTHOLD[31:0]) register.
BitField.name: CNTHOLD

BitField.description: Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter Index Latch\nWhen the IDXF (QEI_STATUS[0]) bit is set, the CNT(QEI_CNT[31:0]) is copied into CNTLATCH (QEI_CNTLATCH[31:0]) register.
BitField.name: CNTLATCH

BitField.description: Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter Compare\n
BitField.name: CNTCMP

BitField.description: Quadrature Encoder Interface Preset Maximum Count\nThis register value determined by user stores the maximum value which may be the number of the QEI counter for the QEI controller compare-counting mode.
BitField.name: CNTMAX

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Reset Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nSetting this bit will enable the WDT time-out reset function if the WDT up counter value has not been cleared after the specific WDT reset delay period expires.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: RSTEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Reset Flag\nThis bit indicates the system has been reset by WDT time-out reset or not.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: RSTF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interrupt Flag\nThis bit will be set to 1 while WDT up counter value reaches the selected WDT time-out interval.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: IF

BitField.description:
WDT Time-out Wake-up Function Control (Write Protect)
If this bit is set to 1, while WDT time-out interrupt flag IF (WDT_CTL[3]) is generated to 1 and interrupt enable bit INTEN (WDT_CTL[6]) is enabled, the WDT time-out interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to chip.
Note 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
Note 2: Chip can be woken up by WDT time-out interrupt signal generated only if WDT clock source is selected to 32 kHz internal low speed RC oscillator (LIRC) or LXT.
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Wake-up Flag \nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of WDT\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: WKF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nIf this bit is enabled, the WDT time-out interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU. \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: WDT Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.\nNote 2: If CWDTEN[2:0] (combined by Config0[31] and Config0[4:3]) bits is not configured to 111, this bit is forced as 1 and user cannot change this bit to 0.
BitField.name: WDTEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interval Selection (Write Protect)\nThese three bits select the time-out interval period for the WDT.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: TOUTSEL

BitField.description: WDT Enable Control SYNC Flag Indicator (Read Only)\nIf user executes enable/disable WDTEN (WDT_CTL[7]), this flag can be indicated enable/disable WDTEN function is completed or not.\nNote: Performing enable or disable WDTEN bit needs 2 * WDT_CLK period to become active.
BitField.name: SYNC

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nWDT up counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
WDT Reset Delay Selection (Write Protect) 
When WDT time-out happened, user has a time named WDT Reset Delay Period to clear WDT counter by programming 0x5AA5 to RSTCNT to prevent WDT time-out reset happened.
User can select a suitable setting of RSTDSEL for different WDT Reset Delay Period.
Note 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
Note 2: This register will be reset to 0 if WDT time-out reset happened.
BitField.name: RSTDSEL

BitField.description: WDT Reset Counter Register\nWriting 0x00005AA5 to this field will reset the internal 20-bit WDT up counter value to 0.\nNote: Performing RSTCNT to reset counter needs 2 * WDT_CLK period to become active.
BitField.name: RSTCNT

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Reset Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nSetting this bit will enable the WDT time-out reset function if the WDT up counter value has not been cleared after the specific WDT reset delay period expires.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
BitField.name: RSTEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Reset Flag\nThis bit indicates the system has been reset by WDT time-out reset or not.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: RSTF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interrupt Flag\nThis bit will be set to 1 while WDT up counter value reaches the selected WDT time-out interval.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: IF

BitField.description:
WDT Time-out Wake-up Function Control (Write Protect)
If this bit is set to 1, while WDT time-out interrupt flag IF (WDT_CTL[3]) is generated to 1 and interrupt enable bit INTEN (WDT_CTL[6]) is enabled, the WDT time-out interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to chip.
Note 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.
Note 2: Chip can be woken up by WDT time-out interrupt signal generated only if WDT clock source is selected to 32 kHz internal low speed RC oscillator (LIRC) or LXT.
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Wake-up Flag \nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of WDT\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: WKF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nIf this bit is enabled, the WDT time-out interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU. \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_RLKTZS register or SYS_RLKTZNS register or SYS_RLKSUBM register.

BitField.description:
Power Switch Interrupt Status
This bit high indicates the RTC_nRWAKE transition from high to low (user pressed the key) when RTC_RPWR is high (stage machine is in Power_On state).
When state machine is not in Power_On state, RTC_nRWAKE transition from high to low will not set this bit high.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit.
BitField.name: PSWST

BitField.description: Key Pressed for 1 Second Interrupt Status\nThis bit high indicates the RTC_nRWAKE kept in low (user pressed the key) for 1 second when RTC_RPWR is high (stage machine is in Power_On state).\nNote: Write 1 to clear this bit.
BitField.name: KPRSST

BitField.description:
Tamper 0 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMP0_PIN detected level non-equal TAMP0LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[9]).
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will be generated again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Clear all TAPMxIF will clear RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL automatically.
BitField.name: TAMP0IF

BitField.description:
Tamper 1 or Pair 0 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMP1_PIN detected level non-equal TAMP1LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[13]) or TAMP0_PIN and TAMP1_PIN disconnected during DYNPR0EN (RTC_TAMPCTL[15]) is activated.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will be generated again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Clear all TAPMxIF will clear RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL automatically.
BitField.name: TAMP1IF
