BitField.description: INT_C\nThis bit is set if INT_C is enabled and if INT_C# pin is in low level. The INT_C# pin is not supported.
BitField.name: INT_C

BitField.description: Re-tuning Event \nThis bit is set if the Re-Tuning Request changes from 0 to 1. Re-Tuning request is not supported.
BitField.name: RE_TUNE_EVENT

BitField.description: FX Event\nThis status is set when R[14] of response register is set to 1 and Response Type R1/R5 is set to 0 in Transfer Mode register. This interrupt is used with response check function.
BitField.name: FX_EVENT

BitField.description: Command Queuing Event\nThis status is set if Command Queuing/Crypto related event has occurred in eMMC/SD mode. Read CQHCI's CQIS/CRNQIS register for more details.
BitField.name: CQE_EVENT

BitField.description: Error Interrupt\nIf any of the bits in the Error Interrupt Status register are set, then this bit is set.
BitField.name: ERR_INTERRUPT

BitField.description: Command Timeout Error\nIn SD/eMMC Mode, this bit is set only if no response is returned within 64 SD clock cycles from the end bit of the command. If the Host Controller detects a CMD line conflict, along with Command CRC Error bit, this bit is set to 1, without waiting for 64 SD/eMMC card clock cycles. \n
BitField.name: CMD_TOUT_ERR

BitField.description:
Command CRC Error 
Command CRC Error is generated in SD/eMMC mode for following two cases. 
If a response is returned and the Command Timeout Error is set to 0 (indicating no timeout), this bit is set to 1 when detecting a CRC error in the command response. 
The Host Controller detects a CMD line conflict by monitoring the CMD line when a command is issued. If the Host Controller drives the CMD line to 1 level, but detects 0 level on the CMD line at the next SD clock edge, then the Host Controller aborts the command (stop driving CMD line) and set this bit to 1. The Command Timeout Error is also set to 1 to distinguish a CMD line conflict.
BitField.name: CMD_CRC_ERR

BitField.description: Command End Bit Error\nThis bit is set when detecting that the end bit of a command response is 0 in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: CMD_END_BIT_ERR

BitField.description: Command Index Error\nThis bit is set if a Command Index error occurs in the command respons in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: CMD_IDX_ERR

BitField.description:
Data Timeout Error
This bit is set in SD/eMMC mode when detecting one of the following timeout conditions: 
Busy timeout for R1b, R5b type 
Busy timeout after Write CRC status 
Write CRC Status timeout 
Read Data timeout
BitField.name: DATA_TOUT_ERR

BitField.description: Data CRC Error\nThis error occurs in SD/eMMC mode when detecting CRC error when transferring read data which uses the DAT line, when detecting the Write CRC status having a value of other than 010 or when write CRC status timeout. \n
BitField.name: DATA_CRC_ERR

BitField.description: Data End Bit Error \nThis error occurs in SD/eMMC mode either when detecting 0 at the end bit position of read data that uses the DAT line or at the end bit position of the CRC status. \n
BitField.name: DATA_END_BIT_ERR

BitField.description: Current Limit Error \nBy setting the SD Bus Power bit in the Power Control register, the Host Controller is requested to supply power for the SD Bus. If the Host Controller supports the Current Limit function, it can be protected from an illegal card by stopping power supply to the card in which case this bit indicates a failure status. A reading of 1 for this bit means that the Host Controller is not supplying power to the SD card due to some failure. A reading of 0 for this bit means that the Host Controller is supplying power and no error has occurred. The Host Controller may require some sampling time to detect the current limit. DWC_mshc Host Controller does not support this function, this bit is always set to 0.\n
BitField.name: CUR_LMT_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD Error \nThis error status is used by Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 in SD/eMMC mode. This bit is set when detecting that any of the bits D00 to D05 in Auto CMD Error Status register has changed from 0 to 1. D07 is effective in case of Auto CMD12. Auto CMD Error Status register is valid while this bit is set to 1 and may be cleared by clearing of this bit. \n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_ERR

BitField.description:
ADMA Error 
This bit is set when the Host Controller detects error during ADMA-based data transfer. The error could be due to following reasons: 
Error response received from System bus (Master I/F) 
ADMA2 Descriptors invalid 
CQE Task or Transfer descriptors invalid 
When the error occurs, the state of the ADMA is saved in the ADMA Error Status register. 
In eMMC CQE mode:
BitField.name: ADMA_ERR

BitField.description: Tuning Error\nThis bit is set when an unrecoverable error is detected in a tuning circuit except during the tuning procedure (occurrence of an error during tuning procedure is indicated by Sampling Clock Select in the Host Control 2 register). By detecting Tuning Error, Host Driver needs to abort a command executing and perform tuning. To reset tuning circuit, Sampling Clock Select is set to 0 before executing tuning procedure. The Tuning Error is higher priority than the other error interrupts generated during data transfer. By detecting Tuning Error, the Host Driver must discard data transferred by a current read/write command and retry data transfer after the Host Controller retrieved from the tuning circuit error. This is applicable in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: TUNING_ERR

BitField.description: Response Error \nHost Controller Version 4.00 supports response error check function to avoid overhead of response error check by Host Driver during DMA execution. If Response Error Check Enable is set to 1 in the Transfer Mode register, Host Controller Checks R1 or R5 response. If an error is detected in a response, this bit is set to 1.This is applicable in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: RESP_ERR

BitField.description: Boot Acknowledgement Error \nThis bit is set when there is a timeout for boot acknowledgement or when detecting boot ack status having a value other than 010. This is applicable only when boot acknowledgement is expected in eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: BOOT_ACK_ERR

BitField.description:
Card Interrupt Status Enable 
If this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Card Interrupt detection is stopped when this bit is cleared and restarted when this bit is set to 1. The Host Driver may clear the Card Interrupt Status Enable before servicing the Card Interrupt and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests from the card are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts. 
By setting this bit to 0, interrupt input must be masked by implementation so that the interrupt input is not affected by external signal in any state (for example, floating).
BitField.name: CARD_INTERRUPT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: INT_A Status Enable \nIf this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Host Driver may clear this bit before servicing the INT_A and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests to INT_A pin are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts.\n
BitField.name: INT_A_STAT_EN

BitField.description: INT_B Status Enable \nIf this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Host Driver may clear this bit before servicing the INT_B and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests to INT_B pin are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts.\n
BitField.name: INT_B_STAT_EN

BitField.description: INT_C Status Enable \nIf this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Host Driver may clear this bit before servicing the INT_C and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests to INT_C pin are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts.\n

BitField.description:
Auto CMD12 Not Executed 
If multiple memory block data transfer is not started due to a command error, this bit is not set because it is not necessary to issue an Auto CMD12. Setting this bit to 1 means that the Host Controller cannot issue Auto CMD12 to stop multiple memory block data transfer, due to some error. If this bit is set to 1, error status bits (D04-D01) is meaningless. 
This bit is set to 0 when Auto CMD Error is generated by Auto CMD23.
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD12_NOT_EXEC

BitField.description:
Auto CMD Timeout Error 
This bit is set if no response is returned with 64 SDCLK cycles from the end bit of the command. 
If this bit is set to 1, error status bits (D04-D01) are meaningless.
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_TOUT_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD CRC Error \nThis bit is set when detecting a CRC error in the command response.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_CRC_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD End Bit Error \nThis bit is set when detecting that the end bit of command response is 0.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_EBIT_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD Index Error \nThis bit is set if the command index error occurs in response to a command.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_IDX_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD Response Error \nThis bit is set when Response Error Check Enable in the Transfer Mode register is set to 1 and an error is detected in R1 response of either Auto CMD12 or CMD13. This status is ignored if any bit between D00 to D04 is set to 1.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_RESP_ERR

BitField.description: This bit of the AUTO_CMD_STAR_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_6

BitField.description:
Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error 
If this bit is set to 1, CMD_wo_DAT is not executed due to an Auto CMD12 Error (D04-D01) in this register. 
This bit is set to 0 when Auto CMD Error is generated by Auto CMD23.
BitField.name: CMD_NOT_ISSUED_AUTO_CMD12

BitField.description: These bits of the AUTO_CMD_STAT_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_15_8

BitField.description:
UHS Mode/eMMC Speed Mode Select
These bits are used to select UHS mode in the SD mode of operation. In eMMC mode, these bits are used to select eMMC Speed mode.
UHS Mode (SD/UHS-II mode only): 
Note: This Host Controller not supports DDR50 and UHS-II mode(SD/UHS-II mode only), please do not set this bit to 0x4 and 0x7.
Note: This Host Controller not supports High Speed DDR and HS400 mode(eMMC mode only), please do not set this bit to 0x4 and 0x7.
BitField.name: UHS_MODE_SEL

BitField.description: 1.8V Signaling Enable \nThis bit controls voltage regulator for I/O cell in UHS-I/eMMC speed modes. Setting this bit from 0 to 1 starts changing the signal voltage from 3.3V to 1.8V. Host Controller clears this bit if switching to 1.8 signaling fails. The value is reflected on the uhs1_swvolt_en pin.\nNote: This bit must be set for all UHS-I speed modes (SDR12/SDR25/SDR50/SDR104/DDR50).
BitField.name: SIGNALING_EN

BitField.description: Driver Strength Select\nThis bit is used to select the Host Controller output driver in 1.8V signaling UHS-I/eMMC speed modes. The bit depends on setting of Preset Value Enable. The value is reflected on the uhs1_drv_sth pin.
BitField.name: DRV_STRENGTH_SEL

BitField.description: Execute Tuning \nThis bit is set to 1 to start the tuning procedure in UHS-I/eMMC speed modes and this bit is automatically cleared when tuning procedure is completed.
BitField.name: EXEC_TUNING

BitField.description: Sampling Clock Select \nThis bit is used by the Host Controller to select the sampling clock in SD/eMMC mode to receive CMD and DAT. This bit is set by the tuning procedure and is valid after the completion of tuning (when Execute Tuning is cleared). Setting this bit to 1 means that tuning is completed successfully and setting this bit to 0 means that tuning has failed. The value is reflected on the sample_cclk_sel pin. \n
BitField.name: SAMPLE_CLK_SEL

BitField.description: UHS-II Interface Enable\nThis bit is used to enable the UHS-II Interface. The value is reflected on the uhs2_if_en pin.\nNote: This Host Controller not supports UHS-II mode, please do not set this bit to 0x1.
BitField.name: UHS2_IF_ENABLE

BitField.description: This bit of the HOST_CTRL2_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_9

BitField.description: ADMA2 Length Mode\nThis bit selects ADMA2 Length mode to be either 16-bit or 26-bit.\n
BitField.name: ADMA2_LEN_MODE

BitField.description: CMD23 Enable\nIf the card supports CMD23, this bit is set to 1. \n
BitField.name: CMD23_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Host Version 4 Enable
This bit selects either Version 3.00 compatible mode or Version 4 mode. 
Functions of following fields are modified for Host Version 4 mode: 
SDMA Address: SDMA uses ADMA System Address (05Fh-058h) instead of SDMA System Address register (003h-000h) 
ADMA2 selection: DMA select in Host Control 1 register 
64-bit ADMA Descriptor Size: 128-bit descriptor is used instead of 96-bit descriptor when 64-bit Addressing is set to 1 
Selection of 32-bit/64-bit System Addressing: Either 32-bit or 64-bit system addressing is selected by 64-bit Addressing bit in this register 
32-bit Block Count: SDMA System Address register (003h-000h) is modified to 32-bit Block Count register
BitField.name: HOST_VER4_ENABLE

BitField.description: 64-bit Addressing\nThis bit is effective when Host Version 4 Enable is set to 1.\n
BitField.name: ADDRESSING

BitField.description: Asynchronous Interrupt Enable\nThis bit can be set if a card supports asynchronous interrupts and Asynchronous Interrupt Support is set to 1 in the Capabilities register\n
BitField.name: ASYNC_INT_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Preset Value Enable
This bit enables automatic selection of SDCLK frequency and Driver strength Preset Value registers. When Preset Value Enable is set, SDCLK frequency generation (Frequency Select and Clock Generator Select) and the driver strength selection are performed by the controller. These values are selected from set of Preset Value registers based on selected speed mode. 
Note: For more information, see the FAQ on Preset Register in the DWC_mshc Databook.
BitField.name: PRESET_VAL_ENABLE

BitField.description: Timeout Clock Frequency \nThis bit shows the base clock frequency used to detect Data Timeout Error. The Timeout Clock unit defines the unit of timeout clock frequency. It can be kHz or MHz. \n
BitField.name: TOUT_CLK_FREQ

BitField.description: This bit of the CAPABILITIES1_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_6

BitField.description: Timeout Clock Unit \nThis bit shows the unit of base clock frequency used to detect Data Timeout Error.\n
BitField.name: TOUT_CLK_UNIT

BitField.description:
Base Clock Frequency for SD clock 
These bits indicate the base (maximum) clock frequency for the SD Clock. The definition of these bits depend on the Host Controller Version. 
6-Bit Base Clock Frequency: This mode is supported by the Host Controller version 1.00 and 2.00. The upper 2 bits are not effective and are always 0. The unit values are 1 MHz. The supported clock range is 10 MHz to 63 MHz. 
If the frequency is 16.5 MHz, the larger value is set to 0001001b (17 MHz) because the Host Driver uses this value to calculate the clock divider value and it does not exceed the upper limit of the SD Clock frequency. If these bits are all 0, the Host system has to get information using a different method.
BitField.name: BASE_CLK_FREQ

BitField.description: Maximum Block Length\nThis bit indicates the maximum block size that the Host driver can read and write to the buffer in the Host Controller. The buffer transfers this block size without wait cycles. The transfer block length is always 512 bytes for the SD Memory irrespective of this bit\n
BitField.name: MAX_BLK_LEN

BitField.description: 8-bit Support for Embedded Device \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller is capable of using an 8-bit bus width mode. This bit is not effective when the Slot Type is set to 10b.\n
BitField.name: Embedded_8_BIT

BitField.description: ADMA2 Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller is capable of using ADMA2.\n
BitField.name: ADMA2_SUPPORT

BitField.description: This bit of the CAPABILITIES1_R is a reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_20

BitField.description: High Speed Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller and the Host System supports High Speed mode and they can supply the SD Clock frequency from 25 MHz to 50 MHz.\n
BitField.name: HIGH_SPEED_SUPPORT

BitField.description: SDMA Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller is capable of using SDMA to transfer data between the system memory and the Host Controller directly.\n
BitField.name: SDMA_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Suspense/Resume Support\nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller supports Suspend/Resume functionality. If this bit is 0, the Host Driver does not issue either Suspend or Resume commands because the Suspend and Resume mechanism is not supported.\n
BitField.name: SUS_RES_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Voltage Support for 3.3V\n
BitField.name: VOLT_33

BitField.description: Voltage Support for SD 3.0V or Embedded 1.2V\n
BitField.name: VOLT_30

BitField.description: Voltage Support for 1.8V\n
BitField.name: VOLT_18

BitField.description: 64-bit System Address Support for V4 \nThis bit sets the Host Controller to support 64-bit System Addressing of V4 mode. When this bit is set to 1, full or part of 64-bit address must be used to decode the Host Controller Registers so that Host Controller Registers can be placed above system memory area. 64-bit address decode of Host Controller registers is effective regardless of setting to 64-bit Addressing in Host Control 2. \n
BitField.name: SYS_ADDR_64_V4

BitField.description:
64-bit System Address Support for V3 
This bit sets the Host controller to support 64-bit System Addressing of V3 mode. 
SDMA cannot be used in 64-bit Addressing in Version 3 Mode.
BitField.name: SYS_ADDR_64_V3

BitField.description: Asynchronous Interrupt Support\nNote: SD Mode only.
BitField.name: ASYNC_INT_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Slot Type \nThese bits indicate usage of a slot by a specific Host System.\n
BitField.name: SLOT_TYPE_R

BitField.description: SDR50 Support\nThis bit indicates that SDR50 is supported. The bit 13 (USE_TUNING_SDR50) indicates whether SDR50 requires tuning or not.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: SDR50_SUPPORT

BitField.description: SDR104 Support \nThis bit mentions that SDR104 requires tuning.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: SDR104_SUPPORT

BitField.description: DDR50 Support\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DDR50_SUPPORT

BitField.description: UHS-II Support\nThis bit indicates whether Host Controller supports UHS-II.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: UHS2_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Driver Type A Support\nThis bit indicates support of Driver Type A for 1.8 Signaling.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DRV_TYPEA

BitField.description: Driver Type C Support\nThis bit indicates support of Driver Type C for 1.8 Signaling.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DRV_TYPEC

BitField.description: Driver Type D Support\nThis bit indicates support of Driver Type D for 1.8 Signaling.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DRV_TYPED

BitField.name: RSVD_39

BitField.description: Timer Count for Re-Tuning\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: RETUNE_CNT

BitField.name: RSVD_44

BitField.description: Use Tuning for SDR50\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: USE_TUNING_SDR50

BitField.description: Re-Tuning Modes\nThese bits select the re-tuning method and limit the maximum data length.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: RE_TUNING_MODES

BitField.description: Clock Multiplier \nThese bits indicate the clock multiplier of the programmable clock generator. Setting these bits to 0 means that the Host Controller does not support a programmable clock generator. \n

BitField.description:

BitField.name: VDD2_18V_SUPPORT

BitField.name: REG_OFFSET_ADDR

BitField.description: Base offset Address for Vendor-Specific registers.
BitField.name: REG_OFFSET_ADDR

BitField.description: Base offset Address for Command Queuing registers.
BitField.name: REG_OFFSET_ADDR

BitField.description: Interrupt signal for each Slot \nThese status bits indicate the logical OR of Interrupt signal and Wakeup signal for each slot. A maximum of 8 slots can be defined. If one interrupt signal is associated with multiple slots, the Host Driver can identify the interrupt that is generated by reading these bits. By a power on reset or by setting Software Reset For All bit, the interrupt signals are de-asserted and this status reads 00h. \nNote: MSHC Host Controller support single card slot. This register shall always return 0.
BitField.name: INTR_SLOT

BitField.description: Specification Version Number\nThese bits indicate the Host controller specification version. The upper and lower 4-bits indicate the version. Values 0x06-0xFF are reserved.
BitField.name: SPEC_VERSION_NUM

BitField.description: Vendor Version Number \nThis field is reserved for the vendor version number. Host Driver must not use this status.
BitField.name: VENDOR_VERSION_NUM

BitField.description: Internal Timer Clock Frequency Value\nThis field scales the frequency of the timer clock provided by ITCFMUL. The Final clock frequency of actual timer clock is calculated as ITCFVAL* ITCFMUL.
BitField.name: ITCFVAL

BitField.description: These bits of the CQCAP register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: CQCCAP_RSVD1

BitField.description: Internal Timer Clock Frequency Multiplier\nThis field indicates the frequency of the clock used for interrupt coalescing timer and for determining the SQS polling period. See ITCFVAL definition for details. Values 0x5 to 0xF are reserved.
BitField.name: ITCFMUL

BitField.description: These bits [27:16] of the CQCAP register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: CQCCAP_RSVD2

BitField.description: Crypto Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller supports cryptographic operations.
BitField.name: CRYPTO_SUPPORT

BitField.description: These bits [31:29] of the CQCAP register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: CQCCAP_RSVD3

BitField.description: Current release number\nThis field indicates the Synopsys DesignWare Cores DWC_mshc/DWC_mshc_lite current release number that is read by an application. \nAn application reading this register in conjunction with the MSHC_VER_TYPE_R register, gathers details of the current release.
BitField.name: MSHC_VER_ID

BitField.description: Current release type\nThis field indicates the Synopsys DesignWare Cores DWC_mshc/DWC_mshc_lite current release type that is read by an application. \nAn application reading this register in conjunction with the MSHC_VER_ID_R register, gathers details of the current release.
BitField.name: MSHC_VER_TYPE

BitField.description:
Command conflict check 
This bit enables command conflict check. 
Note: DWC_mshc controller monitors the CMD line whenever a command is issued and checks whether the value driven on sd_cmd_out matches the value on sd_cmd_in at next subsequent edge of cclk_tx to determine command conflict error. This bit is cleared only if the feed back delay (including I/O Pad delay) is more than (t_card_clk_period - t_setup), where t_setup is the setup time of a flop in DWC_mshc. The I/O pad delay is consistent across CMD and DATA lines, and it is within the value:
(2*t_card_clk_period - t_setup)
BitField.name: CMD_CONFLICT_CHECK

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD1) of the MSHC_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD1

BitField.description: Internal clock gating disable control \nThis bit must be used to disable IP's internal clock gating when required. when disabled clocks are not gated. Clocks to the core (except hclk) must be stopped when programming this bit.
BitField.name: SW_CG_DIS

BitField.description: Undefined INCR Burst \nControls generation of undefined length INCR transfer on Master interface.
BitField.name: UNDEFL_INCR_EN

BitField.description: INCR4 Burst \nControls generation of INCR4 transfers on Master interface.
BitField.name: BURST_INCR4_EN

BitField.description: INCR8 Burst \nControls generation of INCR8 transfers on Master interface.
BitField.name: BURST_INCR8_EN

BitField.description: INCR16 Burst \nControls generation of INCR16 transfers on Master interface.
BitField.name: BURST_INCR16_EN

BitField.description: eMMC Card present\nThis bit indicates the type of card connected. An application program this bit based on the card connected to MSHC.
BitField.name: CARD_IS_EMMC

BitField.description: Disable Data CRC Check\nThis bit controls masking of CRC16 error for Card Write in eMMC mode. This is useful in bus testing (CMD19) for an eMMC device. In bus testing, an eMMC card does not send CRC status for a block, which may generate CRC error. This CRC error can be masked using this bit during bus testing.
BitField.name: DISABLE_DATA_CRC_CHK

BitField.description: EMMC Device Reset signal control\nThis register field controls the sd_rst_n output of DWC_mshc
BitField.name: EMMC_RST_N

BitField.description: Output Enable control for EMMC Device Reset signal PAD control\nThis field drived sd_rst_n_oe output of DWC_mshc
BitField.name: EMMC_RST_N_OE

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD) of the EMMC_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD

BitField.description: Mandatory Boot Enable\nThis bit is used to initiate the mandatory boot operation. The application sets this bit along with VALIDATE_BOOT bit. Writing 0 is ignored. The DWC_mshc clears this bit after the boot transfer is completed or terminated.\n
BitField.name: MAN_BOOT_EN

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD _6_1) of the BOOT_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_6_1

BitField.description: Validate Mandatory Boot Enable bit\nThis bit is used to validate the MAN_BOOT_EN bit.
BitField.name: VALIDATE_BOOT

BitField.description: Boot Acknowledge Enable\nWhen this bit set, DWC_mshc checks for boot acknowledge start pattern of 0-1-0 during boot operation. This bit is applicable for both mandatory and alternate boot mode.
BitField.name: BOOT_ACK_ENABLE

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD_11_9) of the BOOT_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_11_9

BitField.description: Boot Ack Timeout Counter Value \nThis value determines the interval by which boot ack timeout (50 ms) is detected when boot ack is expected during boot operation. \n
BitField.name: BOOT_TOUT_CNT

BitField.description: Setting this bit enables Auto tuning engine This bit is enabled by default when core is configured with mode3 retuning support Clear this bit to 0 when core is configured to have Mode3 re-tuning but SW wishes to disable mode3 re-tuning \nThis field should be programmed only when CLK_CTRL_R.SD_CLK_EN is 0. \n
BitField.name: AT_EN

BitField.description: Select the interval when the corrected center phase select code can be driven on tuning_cclk_sel output.\n
BitField.name: CI_SEL

BitField.description:
Sampling window Threshold enable 
Selects the tuning mode 
Field should be programmed only when SAMPLE_CLK_SEL is '0'
BitField.name: SWIN_TH_EN

BitField.description: Framing errors are not generated when executing tuning. This debug bit allows users to report these errors.\n
BitField.name: RPT_TUNE_ERR

BitField.description: Enable software-managed tuning flow\n
BitField.name: SW_TUNE_EN

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD2) of the AT_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSDV2

BitField.description: This field sets the phase for Left and Right edges for drift monitoring [Left edge offset + Right edge offset] must not be less than total taps of delayLine.\n
BitField.name: WIN_EDGE_SEL

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD3) of the AT_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSDV3

BitField.description: Clock stopping control for Tuning and auto-tuning circuit \nWhen enabled, clock gate control output of DWC_mshc (clk2card_on) is pulled low before changing phase select codes on tuning_cclk_sel and autotuning_cclk_sel. This effectively stops the Device/Card clock, cclk_rx and also drift_cclk_rx. Changing phase code when clocks are stopped ensures glitch free phase switching. Set this bit to 0 if the PHY or delayline can guarantee glitch free switching.\n
BitField.name: TUNE_CLK_STOP_EN

BitField.description: Maximum Latency specification between cclk_tx and cclk_rx \n
BitField.name: PRE_CHANGE_DLY

BitField.description: Time taken for phase switching and stable clock output\nSpecifies the maximum time (in terms of cclk cycles) that the delay line can take to switch its output phase after a change in tuning_cclk_sel or autotuning_cclk_sel. \n
BitField.name: POST_CHANGE_DLY

BitField.description:
Sampling window threshold value setting
The maximum value that can be set here depends on the length of delayline used for tuning. A delayLine with 128 taps can use values from 0x0 to 0x7F.
This field is valid only when SWIN_TH_EN is '1'. Should be programmed only when SAMPLE_CLK_SEL is '0'
BitField.name: SWIN_TH_VAL

BitField.description: Centered Phase code \nReading this field returns the current value on tuning_cclk_sel output Setting AT_CTRL_R.SW_TUNE_EN enables software to write to this field and its contents are reflected on tuning_cclk_sel.\n
BitField.name: CENTER_PH_CODE

BitField.description: Right Edge Phase code \nReading this field returns the phase code value used by Auto-tuning engine to sample data on Right edge of sampling window.
BitField.name: R_EDGE_PH_CODE

BitField.description: Left Edge Phase code \nReading this field returns the phase code value used by Auto-tuning engine to sample data on Left edge of sampling window.
BitField.name: L_EDGE_PH_CODE

BitField.description: These bits of the AT_STAT_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSDV1

BitField.description: Number of Clock Pins\nThis field indicates support of clock pins to select one of devices for shared bus system. Up to 7 clock pins can be supported. \nNote: SD Mode.
BitField.name: NUM_CLK_PIN

BitField.description: This bit (RSVD_3) of the EMBEDDED_CTRL_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_3

BitField.description: Number of Interrupt Input Pins \nThis field indicates support of interrupt input pins for an embedded system.
BitField.name: NUM_INT_PIN

BitField.description: These bits (RSVD_7_6) of the EMBEDDED_CTRL_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_7_6

BitField.description: Bus Width Preset\nEach bit of this field specifies the bus width for each embedded device. The shared bus supports mixing of 4-bit and 8-bit bus width devices. \nNote: SD Mode.
BitField.name: BUS_WIDTH_PRESET

BitField.description: This bit (RSVD_15) of the EMBEDDED_CTRL_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_15

BitField.description: Clock Pin Select \nThis bit is selected by one of clock pin outputs. \nNote: SD Mode.
BitField.name: CLK_PIN_SEL

BitField.description: This bit (RSVD_19) of the EMBEDDED_CTRL_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_19

BitField.description: Interrupt Pin Select \nThese bits enable the interrupt pin inputs. \n
BitField.name: INT_PIN_SEL

BitField.description: This bit (RSVD_23) of the EMBEDDED_CTRL_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_23

BitField.description: Back-End Power Control \nEach bit of this field controls back-end power supply for an embedded device. \nNote: SD Mode
BitField.name: BACK_END_PWR_CTRL

BitField.description: This bit (RSVD_31) of the EMBEDDED_CTRL_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_31

BitField.description: 32-bit Block Count\nThis register must be programmed with a non-zero value for data transfer if the 32-bit Block count register is used instead of the 16-bit Block count register.
BitField.name: BLOCKCNT_SDMASA

BitField.description: Transfer Block Size\nThese bits specify the block size of data transfers. In case of memory, it is set to 512 bytes. It can be accessed only if no transaction is executing. Read operations during transfers may return an invalid value, and write operations are ignored. Following are the values for XFER_BLOCK_SIZE: \nNote: This register must be programmed with a non-zero value for data transfer.
BitField.name: XFER_BLOCK_SIZE

BitField.description: SDMA Buffer Boundary\nThese bits specify the size of contiguous buffer in system memory. The SDMA transfer waits at every boundary specified by these fields and the Host Controller generates the DMA interrupt to request the Host Driver to update the SDMA System Address register.\n
BitField.name: SDMA_BUF_BDARY

BitField.description: This bit of the BLOCKSIZE_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_BLOCKSIZE15

BitField.description:
16-bit Block Count 
If the Host Version 4 Enable bit is set 0 or the 16-bit Block Count register is set to non-zero, the 16-bit Block Count register is selected. 
If the Host Version 4 Enable bit is set 1 and the 16-bit Block Count register is set to zero, the 32-bit Block Count register is selected. 
Following are the values for BLOCK_CNT:
BitField.name: BLOCK_CNT

BitField.description: Command Argument\nThese bits specify the SD/eMMC command argument that is specified in bits 39-8 of the Command format.
BitField.name: ARGUMENT

BitField.description: DMA Enable\nThis bit enables the DMA functionality. If this bit is set to 1, a DMA operation begins when the Host Driver writes to the Command register. You can select one of the DMA modes by using DMA Select in the Host Control 1 register.\n
BitField.name: DMA_ENABLE

BitField.description: Block Count Enable\nThis bit is used to enable the Block Count register, which is relevant for multiple block transfers. If this bit is set to 0, the Block Count register is disabled, which is useful in executing an infinite transfer. The Host Driver must set this bit to 0 when ADMA is used.\n
BitField.name: BLOCK_COUNT_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Auto Command Enable
This field determines use of Auto Command functions. 
Note: In SDIO, this field must be set as 00b (Auto Command Disabled).
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_ENABLE

BitField.description: Data Transfer Direction Select\nThis bit defines the direction of DAT line data transfers. This bit is set to 1 by the Host Driver to transfer data from the SD/eMMC card to the Host Controller and it is set to 0 for all other commands.\n
BitField.name: DATA_XFER_DIR

BitField.description: Multi/Single Block Select\nThis bit is set when issuing multiple-block transfer commands using the DAT line. If this bit is set to 0, it is not necessary to set the Block Count register.\n
BitField.name: MULTI_BLK_SEL

BitField.description:
Response Type R1/R5
This bit selects either R1 or R5 as a response type when the Response Error Check is selected.
Error statuses checked in R1: 
OUT_OF_RANGE 
ADDRESS_ERROR 
BLOCK_LEN_ERROR 
WP_VIOLATION 
CARD_IS_LOCKED 
COM_CRC_ERROR 
CARD_ECC_FAILED 
CC_ERROR 
ERROR 
Response Flags checked in R5: 
COM_CRC_ERROR 
ERROR 
FUNCTION_NUMBER 
OUT_OF_RANGE
BitField.name: RESP_TYPE

BitField.description:
Response Error Check Enable
The Host Controller supports response check function to avoid overhead of response error check by Host driver. Response types of only R1 and R5 can be checked by the Controller. If the Host Controller checks the response error, set this bit to 1 and set Response Interrupt Disable to 1. If an error is detected, the Response Error interrupt is generated in the Error Interrupt Status register. 
Note: 
Response error check must not be enabled for any response type other than R1 and R5. 
Response check must not be enabled for the tuning command.
BitField.name: RESP_ERR_CHK_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Response Interrupt Disable
The Host Controller supports response check function to avoid overhead of response error check by the Host driver. Response types of only R1 and R5 can be checked by the Controller.
If Host Driver checks the response error, set this bit to 0 and wait for Command Complete Interrupt and then check the response register.
If the Host Controller checks the response error, set this bit to 1 and set the Response Error Check Enable bit to 1. The Command Complete Interrupt is disabled by this bit regardless of the Command Complete Signal Enable. 
Note: During tuning (when the Execute Tuning bit in the Host Control2 register is set), the Command Complete Interrupt is not generated irrespective of the Response Interrupt Disable setting.
BitField.name: RESP_INT_DISABLE

BitField.description: These bits of the XFER_MODE_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD

BitField.description: Response Type Select\nThis bit indicates the type of response expected from the card.
BitField.name: RESP_TYPE_SELECT

BitField.description: Sub Command Flag\nThis bit distinguishes between a main command and a sub command.
BitField.name: SUB_CMD_FLAG

BitField.description:
Command CRC Check Enable
This bit enables the Host Controller to check the CRC field in the response. If an error is detected, it is reported as a Command CRC error. 
Note: CRC Check enable must be set to 0 for the command with no response, R3 response, and R4 response. 
For the tuning command, this bit must always be set to 1 to enable the CRC check.
BitField.name: CMD_CRC_CHK_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Command Index Check Enable
This bit enables the Host Controller to check the index field in the response to verify if it has the same value as the command index. If the value is not the same, it is reported as a Command Index error. 
Note: 
Index Check enable must be set to 0 for the command with no response, R2 response, R3 response and R4 response. 
For the tuning command, this bit must always be set to enable the index check.
BitField.name: CMD_IDX_CHK_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Data Present Select
This bit is set to 1 to indicate that data is present and that the data is transferred using the DAT line. This bit is set to 0 in the following instances: 
Command using the CMD line 
Command with no data transfer but using busy signal on the DAT[0] line 
Resume Command
BitField.name: DATA_PRESENT_SEL

BitField.description: Command Type\nThese bits indicate the command type. \nNote: While issuing Abort CMD using CMD12/CMD52 or reset CMD using CMD0/CMD52, CMD_TYPE field shall be set to 0x3.
BitField.name: CMD_TYPE

BitField.description: Command Index\nThese bits are set to the command number that is specified in bits 45-40 of the Command Format.
BitField.name: CMD_INDEX

BitField.description: These bits of the CMD_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD

BitField.description: Command Response \nThese bits reflect 39-8 bits of SD/eMMC Response Field. \nNote: For Auto CMD, the 32-bit response (bits 39-8 of the Response Field) is updated in the RESP67_R register.
BitField.name: RESP01

BitField.description: Command Response\nThese bits reflect 71-40 bits of the SD/eMMC Response Field.
BitField.name: RESP23

BitField.description: Command Response \nThese bits reflect 103-72 bits of the Response Field.
BitField.name: RESP45

BitField.description: Command Response \nThese bits reflect bits 135-104 of SD/EMMC Response Field. \nNote: For Auto CMD, this register also reflects the 32-bit response (bits 39-8 of the Response Field).
BitField.name: RESP67

BitField.description: Buffer Data\nThese bits enable access to the Host Controller packet buffer.
BitField.name: BUF_DATA

BitField.description: Command Inhibit\nThis bit indicates the following : \nSD/eMMC mode: If this bit is set to 0, it indicates that the CMD line is not in use and the Host controller can issue an SD/eMMC command using the CMD line. This bit is set when the command register is written. This bit is cleared when the command response is received. This bit is not cleared by the response of auto CMD12/23 but cleared by the response of read/write command.
BitField.name: CMD_INHIBIT

BitField.description: Command Inhibit DAT\nThis bit is applicable for SD/eMMC mode and is generated if either DAT line active or Read transfer active is set to 1. If this bit is set to 0, it indicates that the Host Controller can issue subsequent SD/eMMC commands.
BitField.name: CMD_INHIBIT_DAT

BitField.description:
DAT Line Active
This bit indicates whether one of the DAT lines on the SD/eMMC bus is in use. 
In the case of read transactions, this bit indicates whether a read transfer is executing on the SD/eMMC bus. 
In the case of write transactions, this bit indicates whether a write transfer is executing on the SD/eMMC bus. 
For a command with busy, this status indicates whether the command executing busy is executing on an SD or eMMC bus.
Note: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: DAT_LINE_ACTIVE

BitField.description: Re-Tuning Request\nDWC_mshc does not generate retuning request. The software must maintain the Retuning timer.
BitField.name: RE_TUNE_REQ

BitField.description: DAT[7:4] Line Signal Level\nThis bit is used to check the DAT line level to recover from errors and for debugging. These bits reflect the value of the sd_dat_in (upper nibble) signal.
BitField.name: DAT_7_4

BitField.description: Write Transfer Active \nThis status indicates whether a write transfer is active for SD/eMMC mode.
BitField.name: WR_XFER_ACTIVE

BitField.description: Read Transfer Active \nThis bit indicates whether a read transfer is active for SD/eMMC mode.
BitField.name: RD_XFER_ACTIVE

BitField.description: Buffer Write Enable\nThis bit is used for non-DMA transfers. This bit is set if space is available for writing data.
BitField.name: BUF_WR_ENABLE

BitField.description: Buffer Read Enable\nThis bit is used for non-DMA transfers. This bit is set if valid data exists in the Host buffer.
BitField.name: BUF_RD_ENABLE

BitField.description: These bits of the PRESENT_STAT_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_15_12

BitField.description: Card Inserted\nThis bit indicates whether a card has been inserted. The Host Controller debounces this signal so that Host Driver need not wait for it to stabilize.
BitField.name: CARD_INSERTED

BitField.description: Card Stable\nThis bit indicates the stability of the Card Detect Pin Level. A card is not detected if this bit is set to 1 and the value of the CARD_INSERTED bit is 0.
BitField.name: CARD_STABLE

BitField.description: Card Detect Pin Level\nThis bit reflects the inverse synchronized value of the card_detect_n signal.
BitField.name: CARD_DETECT_PIN_LEVEL

BitField.description: Write Protect Switch Pin Level\nThis bit is supported only for memory and combo cards. This bit reflects the synchronized value of the card_write_prot signal.
BitField.name: WR_PROTECT_SW_LVL

BitField.description: DAT[3:0] Line Signal Level\nThis bit is used to check the DAT line level to recover from errors and for debugging. These bits reflect the value of the sd_dat_in (lower nibble) signal.
BitField.name: DAT_3_0

BitField.description: Command-Line Signal Level\nThis bit is used to check the CMD line level to recover from errors and for debugging. These bits reflect the value of the sd_cmd_in signal.
BitField.name: CMD_LINE_LVL

BitField.description: Host Regulator Voltage Stable\nThis bit is used to check whether the host regulator voltage is stable for switching the voltage of UHS-I mode. This bit reflects the synchronized value of the host_reg_vol_stable signal.
BitField.name: HOST_REG_VOL

BitField.description: This bit of the PRESENT_ST_R register is reserved bits and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_26

BitField.description: Command Not Issued by Error\nThis bit is set if a command cannot be issued after setting the command register due to an error except the Auto CMD12 error.
BitField.name: CMD_ISSUE_ERR

BitField.description: Sub Command Status\nThis bit is used to distinguish between a main command and a sub command status.
BitField.name: SUB_CMD_STAT

BitField.description: In Dormant Status\nFor SD/eMMC mode, this bit always returns 0.
BitField.name: IN_DORMANT_ST

BitField.description: Lane Synchronization\nFor SD/eMMC mode, this bit always returns 0.
BitField.name: LANE_SYNC

BitField.description: UHS-II Interface Detection\nFor SD/eMMC mode, this bit always returns 0.
BitField.name: UHS2_IF_DETECT

BitField.description: LED Control\nThis bit is used to caution the user not to remove the card while the SD card is being accessed. The value is reflected on the led_control signal.\nNote: This bit is unused, do not set this bit to 0x1.
BitField.name: LED_CTRL

BitField.description: Data Transfer Width \nFor SD/eMMC mode, this bit selects the data transfer width of the Host Controller. The Host Driver sets it to match the data width of the SD/eMMC card.
BitField.name: DAT_XFER_WIDTH

BitField.description: High Speed Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: HIGH_SPEED_EN

BitField.description: DMA Select\n
BitField.name: DMA_SEL

BitField.description: Extended Data Transfer Width \nThis bit controls 8-bit bus width mode of embedded device.
BitField.name: EXT_DAT_XFER

BitField.description: Card Detect Test Level\nThis bit is enabled while the Card Detect Signal Selection is set to 1 and it indicates whether a card inserted or not.
BitField.name: CARD_DETECT_TEST_LVL

BitField.description: Card Detect Signal Selection\nThis bit selects a source for card detection. When the source for the card detection is switched, the interrupt must be disabled during the switching period.
BitField.name: CARD_DETECT_SIG_SEL

BitField.description: SD Bus Power for VDD1 \nThis bit enables VDD1 power of the card. This setting is available on the sd_vdd1_on output of DWC_mshc so that it can be used to control the VDD1 power supply of the card. Before setting this bit, the SD Host Driver sets the SD Bus Voltage Select bit. If the Host Controller detects a No Card state, this bit is cleared. \nIn SD mode, if this bit is cleared, the Host Controller stops the SD Clock by clearing the SD_CLK_IN bit in the CLK_CTRL_R register.
BitField.name: SD_BUS_PWR_VDD1

BitField.description: SD Bus Voltage Select for VDD1/eMMC Bus Voltage Select for VDD \n
BitField.name: SD_BUS_VOL_VDD1

BitField.description: SD Bus Power for VDD2\nThis is irrelevant for SD/eMMC card. \n
BitField.name: SD_BUS_PWR_VDD2

BitField.description: SD Bus Voltage Select for VDD2\nThis is irrelevant for SD/eMMC card.\n
BitField.name: SD_BUS_VOL_VDD2

BitField.description: Stop At Block Gap Request\nThis bit is used to stop executing read and write transactions at the next block gap for non-DMA, SDMA, and ADMA transfers.
BitField.name: STOP_BG_REQ

BitField.description: Continue Request\nThis bit is used to restart the transaction, which was stopped using the Stop At Block Gap Request. The Host Controller automatically clears this bit when the transaction restarts. If stop at block gap request is set to 1, any write to this bit is ignored.
BitField.name: CONTINUE_REQ

BitField.description: Read Wait Control\nThis bit is used to enable the read wait protocol to stop read data using DAT[2] line if the card supports read wait. Otherwise, the Host Controller has to stop the card clock to hold the read data.
BitField.name: RD_WAIT_CTRL

BitField.description: Interrupt At Block Gap \nThis bit is valid only in the 4-bit mode of an SDIO card and is used to select a sample point in the interrupt cycle. Setting to 1 enables interrupt detection at the block gap for a multiple block transfer.
BitField.name: INT_AT_BGAP

BitField.description: These bits of the Block Gap Control register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_7_4

BitField.description: Wakeup Event Enable on Card Interrupt \nThis bit enables wakeup event through a Card Interrupt assertion in the Normal Interrupt Status register. This bit can be set to 1 if FN_WUS (Wake Up Support) in CIS is set to 1.
BitField.name: CARD_INT

BitField.description: Wakeup Event Enable on SD Card Insertion \nThis bit enables wakeup event through Card Insertion assertion in the Normal Interrupt Status register. FN_WUS (Wake Up Support) in CIS does not affect this bit.
BitField.name: CARD_INSERT

BitField.description: Wakeup Event Enable on SD Card Removal \nThis bit enables wakeup event through Card Removal assertion in the Normal Interrupt Status register. For the SDIO card, Wake Up Support (FN_WUS) in the Card Information Structure (CIS) register does not affect this bit.
BitField.name: CARD_REMOVAL

BitField.description: These bits of Wakeup Control register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_7_3

BitField.description: Internal Clock Enable\nThis bit is set to 0 when the Host Driver is not using the Host Controller or the Host Controller awaits a wakeup interrupt. The Host Controller must stop its internal clock to enter a very low power state. However, registers can still be read and written to. The value is reflected on the intclk_en signal. \nNote: If this bit is not used to control the internal clock (base clock and master clock), it is recommended to set this bit to '1' .
BitField.name: INTERNAL_CLK_EN

BitField.description: Internal Clock Stable\nThis bit enables the Host Driver to check the clock stability twice after the Internal Clock Enable bit is set and after the PLL Enable bit is set. This bit reflects the synchronized value of the intclk_stable signal after the Internal Clock Enable bit is set to 1 and also reflects the synchronized value of the card_clk_stable signal after the PLL Enable bit is set to 1.
BitField.name: INTERNAL_CLK_STABLE

BitField.description: SD/eMMC Clock Enable\nThis bit stops the SDCLK or RCLK when set to 0. The SDCLK/RCLK Frequency Select bit can be changed when this bit is set to 0. The value is reflected on the clk2card_on pin.
BitField.name: SD_CLK_EN

BitField.description: PLL Enable\n0x0 (FALSE): PLL is in low power mode \n
BitField.name: PLL_ENABLE

BitField.description: This bit of the CLK_CTRL_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_4

BitField.description: Clock Generator Select\n
BitField.name: CLK_GEN_SELECT

BitField.description: These bits specify the upper 2 bits of 10-bit SDCLK/RCLK Frequency Select control The value is reflected on the upper 2 bits of the card_clk_freq_sel signal.
BitField.name: UPPER_FREQ_SEL

BitField.description: SDCLK/RCLK Frequency Select\n
BitField.name: FREQ_SEL

BitField.description: Data Timeout Counter Value \nThis value determines the interval by which DAT line timeouts are detected. The Timeout clock frequency is generated by dividing the base clock TMCLK value by this value. When setting this register, prevent inadvertent timeout events by clearing the Data Timeout Error Status Enable (in the Error Interrupt Status Enable register). The values for these bits are: \nNote: During a boot operating in an eMMC mode, an application must configure the boot data timeout value (approximately 1 sec) in this bit.
BitField.name: TOUT_CNT

BitField.description: These bits of the Timeout Control register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_7_4

BitField.description: Software Reset For All\nThis reset affects the entire Host Controller except for the card detection circuit. During its initialization, the Host Driver sets this bit to 1 to reset the Host Controller. All registers are reset except the capabilities register. If this bit is set to 1, the Host Driver must issue reset command and reinitialize the card.
BitField.name: SW_RST_ALL

BitField.description:
Software Reset For CMD line 
This bit resets only a part of the command circuit to be able to issue a command. This reset is effective only for a command issuing circuit (including response error statuses related to Command Inhibit (CMD) control) and does not affect the data transfer circuit. Host Controller can continue data transfer even after this reset is executed while handling subcommand-response errors. 
The following registers and bits are cleared by this bit: 
Present State register : Command Inhibit (CMD) bit 
Normal Interrupt Status register : Command Complete bit 
Error Interrupt Status : Response error statuses related to Command Inhibit (CMD) bit
BitField.name: SW_RST_CMD

BitField.description:
Software Reset For DAT line 
This bit is used in SD/eMMC mode and it resets only a part of the data circuit and the DMA circuit is also reset. 
The following registers and bits are cleared by this bit: 
Buffer Data Port register 
Buffer is cleared and initialized. 
Present state register 
Buffer Read Enable 
Buffer Write Enable 
Read Transfer Active 
Write Transfer Active 
DAT Line Active 
Command Inhibit (DAT) 
Block Gap Control register 
Continue Request 
Stop At Block Gap Request 
Normal Interrupt status register 
Buffer Read Ready 
Buffer Write Ready 
DMA Interrupt 
Block Gap Event 
Transfer Complete
BitField.name: SW_RST_DAT

BitField.description: These bits of the SW_RST_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_7_3

BitField.description: Command Complete\nIn an SD/eMMC Mode, this bit is set when the end bit of a response except for Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23. \nThis interrupt is not generated when the Response Interrupt Disable in Transfer Mode Register is set to 1.
BitField.name: CMD_COMPLETE

BitField.description: Transfer Complete\nThis bit is set when a read/write transfer and a command with status busy is completed.
BitField.name: XFER_COMPLETE

BitField.description: Block Gap Event\nThis bit is set when both read/write transaction is stopped at block gap due to a Stop at Block Gap Request.
BitField.name: BGAP_EVENT

BitField.description: DMA Interrupt\nThis bit is set if the Host Controller detects the SDMA Buffer Boundary during transfer. In case of ADMA, by setting the Int field in the descriptor table, the Host controller generates this interrupt. This interrupt is not generated after a Transfer Complete.
BitField.name: DMA_INTERRUPT

BitField.description: Buffer Write Ready\nThis bit is set if the Buffer Write Enable changes from 0 to 1.
BitField.name: BUF_WR_READY

BitField.description: Buffer Read Ready\nThis bit is set if the Buffer Read Enable changes from 0 to 1.
BitField.name: BUF_RD_READY

BitField.description: Card Insertion\nThis bit is set if the Card Inserted in the Present State register changes from 0 to 1.
BitField.name: CARD_INSERTION

BitField.description: Card Removal\nThis bit is set if the Card Inserted in the Present State register changes from 1 to 0.
BitField.name: CARD_REMOVAL

BitField.description:
Card Interrupt
This bit reflects the synchronized value of: 
DAT[1] Interrupt Input for SD Mode 
DAT[2] Interrupt Input for UHS-II Mode
BitField.name: CARD_INTERRUPT

BitField.description: INT_A\nThis bit is set if INT_A is enabled and if INT_A# pin is in low level. The INT_A# pin is not supported.
BitField.name: INT_A

BitField.description: INT_B\nThis bit is set if INT_B is enabled and if INT_B# pin is in low level. The INT_B# pin is not supported.
BitField.name: INT_B

BitField.description: INT_C\nThis bit is set if INT_C is enabled and if INT_C# pin is in low level. The INT_C# pin is not supported.
BitField.name: INT_C

BitField.description: Re-tuning Event \nThis bit is set if the Re-Tuning Request changes from 0 to 1. Re-Tuning request is not supported.
BitField.name: RE_TUNE_EVENT

BitField.description: FX Event\nThis status is set when R[14] of response register is set to 1 and Response Type R1/R5 is set to 0 in Transfer Mode register. This interrupt is used with response check function.
BitField.name: FX_EVENT

BitField.description: Command Queuing Event\nThis status is set if Command Queuing/Crypto related event has occurred in eMMC/SD mode. Read CQHCI's CQIS/CRNQIS register for more details.
BitField.name: CQE_EVENT

BitField.description: Error Interrupt\nIf any of the bits in the Error Interrupt Status register are set, then this bit is set.
BitField.name: ERR_INTERRUPT

BitField.description: Command Timeout Error\nIn SD/eMMC Mode, this bit is set only if no response is returned within 64 SD clock cycles from the end bit of the command. If the Host Controller detects a CMD line conflict, along with Command CRC Error bit, this bit is set to 1, without waiting for 64 SD/eMMC card clock cycles. \n
BitField.name: CMD_TOUT_ERR

BitField.description:
Command CRC Error 
Command CRC Error is generated in SD/eMMC mode for following two cases. 
If a response is returned and the Command Timeout Error is set to 0 (indicating no timeout), this bit is set to 1 when detecting a CRC error in the command response. 
The Host Controller detects a CMD line conflict by monitoring the CMD line when a command is issued. If the Host Controller drives the CMD line to 1 level, but detects 0 level on the CMD line at the next SD clock edge, then the Host Controller aborts the command (stop driving CMD line) and set this bit to 1. The Command Timeout Error is also set to 1 to distinguish a CMD line conflict.
BitField.name: CMD_CRC_ERR

BitField.description: Command End Bit Error\nThis bit is set when detecting that the end bit of a command response is 0 in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: CMD_END_BIT_ERR

BitField.description: Command Index Error\nThis bit is set if a Command Index error occurs in the command respons in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: CMD_IDX_ERR

BitField.description:
Data Timeout Error
This bit is set in SD/eMMC mode when detecting one of the following timeout conditions: 
Busy timeout for R1b, R5b type 
Busy timeout after Write CRC status 
Write CRC Status timeout 
Read Data timeout
BitField.name: DATA_TOUT_ERR

BitField.description: Data CRC Error\nThis error occurs in SD/eMMC mode when detecting CRC error when transferring read data which uses the DAT line, when detecting the Write CRC status having a value of other than 010 or when write CRC status timeout. \n
BitField.name: DATA_CRC_ERR

BitField.description: Data End Bit Error \nThis error occurs in SD/eMMC mode either when detecting 0 at the end bit position of read data that uses the DAT line or at the end bit position of the CRC status. \n
BitField.name: DATA_END_BIT_ERR

BitField.description: Current Limit Error \nBy setting the SD Bus Power bit in the Power Control register, the Host Controller is requested to supply power for the SD Bus. If the Host Controller supports the Current Limit function, it can be protected from an illegal card by stopping power supply to the card in which case this bit indicates a failure status. A reading of 1 for this bit means that the Host Controller is not supplying power to the SD card due to some failure. A reading of 0 for this bit means that the Host Controller is supplying power and no error has occurred. The Host Controller may require some sampling time to detect the current limit. DWC_mshc Host Controller does not support this function, this bit is always set to 0.\n
BitField.name: CUR_LMT_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD Error \nThis error status is used by Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 in SD/eMMC mode. This bit is set when detecting that any of the bits D00 to D05 in Auto CMD Error Status register has changed from 0 to 1. D07 is effective in case of Auto CMD12. Auto CMD Error Status register is valid while this bit is set to 1 and may be cleared by clearing of this bit. \n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_ERR

BitField.description:
ADMA Error 
This bit is set when the Host Controller detects error during ADMA-based data transfer. The error could be due to following reasons: 
Error response received from System bus (Master I/F) 
ADMA2 Descriptors invalid 
CQE Task or Transfer descriptors invalid 
When the error occurs, the state of the ADMA is saved in the ADMA Error Status register. 
In eMMC CQE mode:
BitField.name: ADMA_ERR

BitField.description: Tuning Error\nThis bit is set when an unrecoverable error is detected in a tuning circuit except during the tuning procedure (occurrence of an error during tuning procedure is indicated by Sampling Clock Select in the Host Control 2 register). By detecting Tuning Error, Host Driver needs to abort a command executing and perform tuning. To reset tuning circuit, Sampling Clock Select is set to 0 before executing tuning procedure. The Tuning Error is higher priority than the other error interrupts generated during data transfer. By detecting Tuning Error, the Host Driver must discard data transferred by a current read/write command and retry data transfer after the Host Controller retrieved from the tuning circuit error. This is applicable in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: TUNING_ERR

BitField.description: Response Error \nHost Controller Version 4.00 supports response error check function to avoid overhead of response error check by Host Driver during DMA execution. If Response Error Check Enable is set to 1 in the Transfer Mode register, Host Controller Checks R1 or R5 response. If an error is detected in a response, this bit is set to 1.This is applicable in SD/eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: RESP_ERR

BitField.description: Boot Acknowledgement Error \nThis bit is set when there is a timeout for boot acknowledgement or when detecting boot ack status having a value other than 010. This is applicable only when boot acknowledgement is expected in eMMC mode. \n
BitField.name: BOOT_ACK_ERR

BitField.description: This bit (VENDOR_ERR1) of the ERROR_INT_STAT_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: VENDOR_ERR1

BitField.description: This bit (VENDOR_ERR2) of the ERROR_INT_STAT_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: VENDOR_ERR2

BitField.description: This bit (VENDOR_ERR3) of the ERROR_INT_STAT_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: VENDOR_ERR3

BitField.description: Command Complete Status Enable\n
BitField.name: CMD_COMPLETE_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Transfer Complete Status Enable\n
BitField.name: XFER_COMPLETE_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Block Gap Event Status Enable\n
BitField.name: BGAP_EVENT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: DMA Interrupt Status Enable \n
BitField.name: DMA_INTERRUPT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Buffer Write Ready Status Enable\n
BitField.name: BUF_WR_READY_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Buffer Read Ready Status Enable\n
BitField.name: BUF_RD_READY_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Card Insertion Status Enable\n
BitField.name: CARD_INSERTION_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Card Removal Status Enable\n
BitField.name: CARD_REMOVAL_STAT_EN

BitField.description:
Card Interrupt Status Enable 
If this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Card Interrupt detection is stopped when this bit is cleared and restarted when this bit is set to 1. The Host Driver may clear the Card Interrupt Status Enable before servicing the Card Interrupt and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests from the card are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts. 
By setting this bit to 0, interrupt input must be masked by implementation so that the interrupt input is not affected by external signal in any state (for example, floating).
BitField.name: CARD_INTERRUPT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: INT_A Status Enable \nIf this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Host Driver may clear this bit before servicing the INT_A and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests to INT_A pin are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts.\n
BitField.name: INT_A_STAT_EN

BitField.description: INT_B Status Enable \nIf this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Host Driver may clear this bit before servicing the INT_B and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests to INT_B pin are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts.\n
BitField.name: INT_B_STAT_EN

BitField.description: INT_C Status Enable \nIf this bit is set to 0, the Host Controller clears the interrupt request to the System. The Host Driver may clear this bit before servicing the INT_C and may set this bit again after all interrupt requests to INT_C pin are cleared to prevent inadvertent interrupts.\n
BitField.name: INT_C_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Re-Tuning Event Status Enable\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: RE_TUNE_EVENT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: FX Event Status Enable \nThis bit is added from Version 4.10.
BitField.name: FX_EVENT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: CQE Event Status Enable\n
BitField.name: CQE_EVENT_STAT_EN

BitField.description: This bit of the NORMAL_INT_STAT_EN_R register is reserved and always returns 0\n
BitField.name: RSVD_15

BitField.description: Command Timeout Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: CMD_TOUT_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Command CRC Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: CMD_CRC_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Command End Bit Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: CMD_END_BIT_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Command Index Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: CMD_IDX_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Data Timeout Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: DATA_TOUT_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Data CRC Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: DATA_CRC_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Data End Bit Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: DATA_END_BIT_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Current Limit Error Status Enable\n
BitField.name: CUR_LMT_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Auto CMD Error Status Enable\nNote: SD/eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: ADMA Error Status Enable\n
BitField.name: ADMA_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Tuning Error Status Enable\nNote: UHS-I Mode only.
BitField.name: TUNING_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Response Error Status Enable\nNote: SD Mode only.
BitField.name: RESP_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description: Boot Acknowledgment Error\nSetting this bit to 1 enables setting of Boot Acknowledgment Error in Error Interrupt Status register (ERROR_INT_STAT_R).\nNote: eMMC Mode only.
BitField.name: BOOT_ACK_ERR_STAT_EN

BitField.description:
Auto CMD12 Not Executed 
If multiple memory block data transfer is not started due to a command error, this bit is not set because it is not necessary to issue an Auto CMD12. Setting this bit to 1 means that the Host Controller cannot issue Auto CMD12 to stop multiple memory block data transfer, due to some error. If this bit is set to 1, error status bits (D04-D01) is meaningless. 
This bit is set to 0 when Auto CMD Error is generated by Auto CMD23.
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD12_NOT_EXEC

BitField.description:
Auto CMD Timeout Error 
This bit is set if no response is returned with 64 SDCLK cycles from the end bit of the command. 
If this bit is set to 1, error status bits (D04-D01) are meaningless.
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_TOUT_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD CRC Error \nThis bit is set when detecting a CRC error in the command response.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_CRC_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD End Bit Error \nThis bit is set when detecting that the end bit of command response is 0.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_EBIT_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD Index Error \nThis bit is set if the command index error occurs in response to a command.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_IDX_ERR

BitField.description: Auto CMD Response Error \nThis bit is set when Response Error Check Enable in the Transfer Mode register is set to 1 and an error is detected in R1 response of either Auto CMD12 or CMD13. This status is ignored if any bit between D00 to D04 is set to 1.\n
BitField.name: AUTO_CMD_RESP_ERR

BitField.description: This bit of the AUTO_CMD_STAR_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_6

BitField.description:
Command Not Issued By Auto CMD12 Error 
If this bit is set to 1, CMD_wo_DAT is not executed due to an Auto CMD12 Error (D04-D01) in this register. 
This bit is set to 0 when Auto CMD Error is generated by Auto CMD23.
BitField.name: CMD_NOT_ISSUED_AUTO_CMD12

BitField.description: These bits of the AUTO_CMD_STAT_R register are reserved and always return 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_15_8

BitField.description:
UHS Mode/eMMC Speed Mode Select
These bits are used to select UHS mode in the SD mode of operation. In eMMC mode, these bits are used to select eMMC Speed mode.
UHS Mode (SD/UHS-II mode only): 
Note: This Host Controller not supports DDR50 and UHS-II mode(SD/UHS-II mode only), please do not set this bit to 0x4 and 0x7.
Note: This Host Controller not supports High Speed DDR and HS400 mode(eMMC mode only), please do not set this bit to 0x4 and 0x7.
BitField.name: UHS_MODE_SEL

BitField.description: 1.8V Signaling Enable \nThis bit controls voltage regulator for I/O cell in UHS-I/eMMC speed modes. Setting this bit from 0 to 1 starts changing the signal voltage from 3.3V to 1.8V. Host Controller clears this bit if switching to 1.8 signaling fails. The value is reflected on the uhs1_swvolt_en pin.\nNote: This bit must be set for all UHS-I speed modes (SDR12/SDR25/SDR50/SDR104/DDR50).
BitField.name: SIGNALING_EN

BitField.description: Driver Strength Select\nThis bit is used to select the Host Controller output driver in 1.8V signaling UHS-I/eMMC speed modes. The bit depends on setting of Preset Value Enable. The value is reflected on the uhs1_drv_sth pin.
BitField.name: DRV_STRENGTH_SEL

BitField.description: Execute Tuning \nThis bit is set to 1 to start the tuning procedure in UHS-I/eMMC speed modes and this bit is automatically cleared when tuning procedure is completed.
BitField.name: EXEC_TUNING

BitField.description: Sampling Clock Select \nThis bit is used by the Host Controller to select the sampling clock in SD/eMMC mode to receive CMD and DAT. This bit is set by the tuning procedure and is valid after the completion of tuning (when Execute Tuning is cleared). Setting this bit to 1 means that tuning is completed successfully and setting this bit to 0 means that tuning has failed. The value is reflected on the sample_cclk_sel pin. \n
BitField.name: SAMPLE_CLK_SEL

BitField.description: UHS-II Interface Enable\nThis bit is used to enable the UHS-II Interface. The value is reflected on the uhs2_if_en pin.\nNote: This Host Controller not supports UHS-II mode, please do not set this bit to 0x1.
BitField.name: UHS2_IF_ENABLE

BitField.description: This bit of the HOST_CTRL2_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_9

BitField.description: ADMA2 Length Mode\nThis bit selects ADMA2 Length mode to be either 16-bit or 26-bit.\n
BitField.name: ADMA2_LEN_MODE

BitField.description: CMD23 Enable\nIf the card supports CMD23, this bit is set to 1. \n
BitField.name: CMD23_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Host Version 4 Enable
This bit selects either Version 3.00 compatible mode or Version 4 mode. 
Functions of following fields are modified for Host Version 4 mode: 
SDMA Address: SDMA uses ADMA System Address (05Fh-058h) instead of SDMA System Address register (003h-000h) 
ADMA2 selection: DMA select in Host Control 1 register 
64-bit ADMA Descriptor Size: 128-bit descriptor is used instead of 96-bit descriptor when 64-bit Addressing is set to 1 
Selection of 32-bit/64-bit System Addressing: Either 32-bit or 64-bit system addressing is selected by 64-bit Addressing bit in this register 
32-bit Block Count: SDMA System Address register (003h-000h) is modified to 32-bit Block Count register
BitField.name: HOST_VER4_ENABLE

BitField.description: 64-bit Addressing\nThis bit is effective when Host Version 4 Enable is set to 1.\n
BitField.name: ADDRESSING

BitField.description: Asynchronous Interrupt Enable\nThis bit can be set if a card supports asynchronous interrupts and Asynchronous Interrupt Support is set to 1 in the Capabilities register\n
BitField.name: ASYNC_INT_ENABLE

BitField.description:
Preset Value Enable
This bit enables automatic selection of SDCLK frequency and Driver strength Preset Value registers. When Preset Value Enable is set, SDCLK frequency generation (Frequency Select and Clock Generator Select) and the driver strength selection are performed by the controller. These values are selected from set of Preset Value registers based on selected speed mode. 
Note: For more information, see the FAQ on Preset Register in the DWC_mshc Databook.
BitField.name: PRESET_VAL_ENABLE

BitField.description: Timeout Clock Frequency \nThis bit shows the base clock frequency used to detect Data Timeout Error. The Timeout Clock unit defines the unit of timeout clock frequency. It can be kHz or MHz. \n
BitField.name: TOUT_CLK_FREQ

BitField.description: This bit of the CAPABILITIES1_R register is reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_6

BitField.description: Timeout Clock Unit \nThis bit shows the unit of base clock frequency used to detect Data Timeout Error.\n
BitField.name: TOUT_CLK_UNIT

BitField.description:
Base Clock Frequency for SD clock 
These bits indicate the base (maximum) clock frequency for the SD Clock. The definition of these bits depend on the Host Controller Version. 
6-Bit Base Clock Frequency: This mode is supported by the Host Controller version 1.00 and 2.00. The upper 2 bits are not effective and are always 0. The unit values are 1 MHz. The supported clock range is 10 MHz to 63 MHz. 
If the frequency is 16.5 MHz, the larger value is set to 0001001b (17 MHz) because the Host Driver uses this value to calculate the clock divider value and it does not exceed the upper limit of the SD Clock frequency. If these bits are all 0, the Host system has to get information using a different method.
BitField.name: BASE_CLK_FREQ

BitField.description: Maximum Block Length\nThis bit indicates the maximum block size that the Host driver can read and write to the buffer in the Host Controller. The buffer transfers this block size without wait cycles. The transfer block length is always 512 bytes for the SD Memory irrespective of this bit\n
BitField.name: MAX_BLK_LEN

BitField.description: 8-bit Support for Embedded Device \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller is capable of using an 8-bit bus width mode. This bit is not effective when the Slot Type is set to 10b.\n
BitField.name: Embedded_8_BIT

BitField.description: ADMA2 Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller is capable of using ADMA2.\n
BitField.name: ADMA2_SUPPORT

BitField.description: This bit of the CAPABILITIES1_R is a reserved and always returns 0.
BitField.name: RSVD_20

BitField.description: High Speed Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller and the Host System supports High Speed mode and they can supply the SD Clock frequency from 25 MHz to 50 MHz.\n
BitField.name: HIGH_SPEED_SUPPORT

BitField.description: SDMA Support \nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller is capable of using SDMA to transfer data between the system memory and the Host Controller directly.\n
BitField.name: SDMA_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Suspense/Resume Support\nThis bit indicates whether the Host Controller supports Suspend/Resume functionality. If this bit is 0, the Host Driver does not issue either Suspend or Resume commands because the Suspend and Resume mechanism is not supported.\n
BitField.name: SUS_RES_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Voltage Support for 3.3V\n
BitField.name: VOLT_33

BitField.description: Voltage Support for SD 3.0V or Embedded 1.2V\n
BitField.name: VOLT_30

BitField.description: Voltage Support for 1.8V\n
BitField.name: VOLT_18

BitField.description: 64-bit System Address Support for V4 \nThis bit sets the Host Controller to support 64-bit System Addressing of V4 mode. When this bit is set to 1, full or part of 64-bit address must be used to decode the Host Controller Registers so that Host Controller Registers can be placed above system memory area. 64-bit address decode of Host Controller registers is effective regardless of setting to 64-bit Addressing in Host Control 2. \n
BitField.name: SYS_ADDR_64_V4

BitField.description:
64-bit System Address Support for V3 
This bit sets the Host controller to support 64-bit System Addressing of V3 mode. 
SDMA cannot be used in 64-bit Addressing in Version 3 Mode.
BitField.name: SYS_ADDR_64_V3

BitField.description: Asynchronous Interrupt Support\nNote: SD Mode only.
BitField.name: ASYNC_INT_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Slot Type \nThese bits indicate usage of a slot by a specific Host System.\n
BitField.name: SLOT_TYPE_R

BitField.description: SDR50 Support\nThis bit indicates that SDR50 is supported. The bit 13 (USE_TUNING_SDR50) indicates whether SDR50 requires tuning or not.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: SDR50_SUPPORT

BitField.description: SDR104 Support \nThis bit mentions that SDR104 requires tuning.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: SDR104_SUPPORT

BitField.description: DDR50 Support\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DDR50_SUPPORT

BitField.description: UHS-II Support\nThis bit indicates whether Host Controller supports UHS-II.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: UHS2_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Driver Type A Support\nThis bit indicates support of Driver Type A for 1.8 Signaling.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DRV_TYPEA

BitField.description: Driver Type C Support\nThis bit indicates support of Driver Type C for 1.8 Signaling.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DRV_TYPEC

BitField.description: Driver Type D Support\nThis bit indicates support of Driver Type D for 1.8 Signaling.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: DRV_TYPED

BitField.name: RSVD_39

BitField.description: Timer Count for Re-Tuning\nNote: UHS-I only.

BitField.name: USE_TUNING_SDR50

BitField.description: Re-Tuning Modes\nThese bits select the re-tuning method and limit the maximum data length.\nNote: UHS-I only.
BitField.name: RE_TUNING_MODES

BitField.description: Clock Multiplier \nThese bits indicate the clock multiplier of the programmable clock generator. Setting these bits to 0 means that the Host Controller does not support a programmable clock generator. \n

BitField.name: RSVD_56_58

BitField.description:
1.8V VDD2 Support 
This bit indicates support of VDD2 for the Host System.
BitField.name: VDD2_18V_SUPPORT

BitField.description: Interrupt signal for each Slot \nThese status bits indicate the logical OR of Interrupt signal and Wakeup signal for each slot. A maximum of 8 slots can be defined. If one interrupt signal is associated with multiple slots, the Host Driver can identify the interrupt that is generated by reading these bits. By a power on reset or by setting Software Reset For All bit, the interrupt signals are de-asserted and this status reads 00h. \nNote: MSHC Host Controller support single card slot. This register shall always return 0.
BitField.name: INTR_SLOT

BitField.description: Internal Timer Clock Frequency Multiplier\nThis field indicates the frequency of the clock used for interrupt coalescing timer and for determining the SQS polling period. See ITCFVAL definition for details. Values 0x5 to 0xF are reserved.
BitField.name: ITCFMUL
